scenario: TaskRabbit 双边市场排序：特征全是表格信号（评分、完成率、历史 booking 率、价格区间），训练样本约 80 万行，PM 要能解释「为什么这个 tasker 排第一」。
scenario_en: TaskRabbit two-sided marketplace ranking: all features are tabular signals (rating, completion rate, past booking rate, price band), about 800k training rows, and the PM must be able to explain why a tasker ranked first.
q: v1 的排序模型该选 XGBoost 还是深度学习？
q_en: For the v1 ranking model, do you pick XGBoost or deep learning?
options: 上一个 Transformer 端到端学，让模型自己从原始字段里学表示，省掉整个特征工程环节
选 XGBoost：表格特征加 80 万行是它主场，特征重要性直接给 PM 解释
做一个双塔神经网络，把 tasker 和 client 各自编成 embedding，用内积打分并复用向量
先不建模，用人工加权规则打分：评分×0.5 + 完成率×0.3 + 价格×0.2，等数据攒够再说
options_en: Go end-to-end with a Transformer so the model learns representations from raw fields and you skip feature engineering entirely.
Pick XGBoost: tabular features and 800k rows are its home turf, and feature importance gives the PM a direct explanation.
Build a two-tower neural net that embeds taskers and clients separately, scores by dot product, and reuses the vectors.
Skip modeling for now: score with hand-weighted rules, rating x0.5 + completion x0.3 + price x0.2, until more data piles up.
tradeoff: XGBoost vs 深度学习：选 XGBoost 得到几分钟一轮的迭代和可解释的特征重要性，代价是学不到文本、图像这类非结构化信号。
why: 特征是表格、样本 80 万行、还要能解释，三条约束同时指向 XGBoost；深度学习要更多数据和 GPU 才追得平。
why_en: Tabular features, under a million rows, and an explainability requirement all point at XGBoost, while deep learning needs far more data and GPU time just to catch up.
whenOtherWins: 如果排序要吃任务描述的自由文本或现场照片，或样本量涨到千万级，深度学习的表示学习才开始赚回它的训练成本。
optionMeanings: 端到端序列模型自动学表示。
梯度提升树吃表格特征。
双塔模型各自编码再算内积。
人工设权重的线性打分。
optionMeanings_en: An end-to-end sequence model that learns representations itself.
A gradient-boosted tree over tabular features.
A two-tower model that encodes each side then takes a dot product.
A linear score with hand-set weights.
optionDirectness: 有海量非结构化输入时才值。
异质表格特征 + 中等样本量的主场。
候选池上百万、要预算向量时才需要。
冷启动没有标签数据时的过渡方案。
optionDirectness_en: Worth it only with massive unstructured input.
Its home turf: heterogeneous tabular features at medium data size.
Needed when the candidate pool is huge and vectors must be precomputed.
A stopgap for cold start with no labels yet.
optionScenarioImpacts: 80 万行喂不饱它，还得配 GPU。
几分钟训一轮，重要性表直接给 PM。
多一套向量索引要维护，收益却看不见。
权重拍脑袋定，没法随反馈自学。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: 800k rows won't feed it, and you still need GPUs.
Minutes per training round, and the importance table goes straight to the PM.
You maintain a vector index for a gain you can't yet see.
Weights are guesses and never learn from feedback.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个梯度提升决策树库，逐棵树拟合上一轮的残差，擅长表格数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XGBoost is a gradient-boosted decision tree library that fits each new tree to the previous round's residuals and excels on tabular data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 树模型统计每个特征在分裂中贡献了多少增益，用来解释模型看重什么。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Feature importance sums how much gain each feature contributed across splits, so you can explain what the model relies on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个对象压成一串稠密数字，使语义相近的对象在向量空间里也靠得近。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding compresses an object into a dense vector so that similar objects land close together in that space.

termDefinitions.meaning: 产品经理，这里指要向他解释排序结果的业务方。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PM stands for product manager, the business stakeholder who needs the ranking explained.

scenario: 同一批排序特征里，价格是连续值、品类是高基数类别、「上次接单距今天数」有 30% 是空的。
scenario_en: In the same ranking feature set, price is continuous, category is high-cardinality, and 30% of "days since last job" values are missing.
q: 在「异质特征 + 缺失值」这一维度上，梯度提升树和神经网络差在哪？
q_en: On the axis of heterogeneous features plus missing values, where do boosted trees and neural nets differ?
options: 两者都必须先做 one-hot 和标准化，差别只在训练速度上，预处理成本是一样的
梯度提升树会给缺失值学一个默认分裂方向，神经网络得先补值再统一量纲
神经网络对缺失更鲁棒，因为 dropout 本身就在模拟特征缺失，所以不用管空值
梯度提升树必须把连续特征离散化成分桶才能用，神经网络可以直接吃原始数值
options_en: Both need one-hot encoding and standardization first; the only difference is training speed, not preprocessing cost.
Boosted trees learn a default split direction for missing values, while a neural net needs imputation and rescaling first.
Neural nets are more robust to missing data because dropout already simulates missing features, so you can ignore nulls.
Boosted trees require bucketizing continuous features first, while a neural net can consume raw numeric values directly.
tradeoff: 梯度提升树 vs 神经网络：树省掉填充和标准化这两步预处理，代价是学不到跨特征的连续表示。
why: 树按增益切分，天然吃得下不同量纲的异质特征，还能给缺失值单独学一条默认分支；神经网络对量纲和空值都很敏感。
why_en: Trees split by gain, so they absorb heterogeneous scales and even learn a default branch for missing values, while a neural net is sensitive to both scale and nulls.
optionMeanings: 认为两者预处理需求相同。
树学默认分支，网络需预处理。
认为 dropout 顶替了缺失值处理。
认为树必须先分桶。
optionMeanings_en: Claims both need the same preprocessing.
Trees learn a default branch; nets need preprocessing.
Claims dropout substitutes for missing-value handling.
Claims trees must bucketize first.
optionDirectness: 对线性模型才成立，树不需要。
正是两类模型的归纳偏置差异。
dropout 是正则化，和输入空值无关。
分桶是树的内部行为，不是输入要求。
optionDirectness_en: True for linear models, not for trees.
This is exactly the inductive-bias difference.
Dropout is regularization, unrelated to null inputs.
Bucketizing is internal to the tree, not an input requirement.
optionScenarioImpacts: 会白白多写一层填充和缩放代码。
30% 空值不用编造填充值。
空值直接进网络会变成 NaN 传播。
手动分桶会丢掉价格的细粒度差异。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You write an imputation and scaling layer for nothing.
The 30% missing values need no invented fill value.
Raw nulls entering a net turn into NaN propagation.
Manual bucketizing throws away fine-grained price differences.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个类别特征展开成一组 0/1 列，每个取值占一列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: One-hot encoding expands a categorical feature into a set of zero-one columns, one per value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时随机置零一部分神经元，用来防止过拟合的正则化手段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dropout randomly zeroes out neurons during training as a regularization trick against overfitting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 浮点里的非数值，一旦进入计算会污染后续所有结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NaN means not a number, a floating-point value that contaminates every later computation once it enters.

scenario: 同一个 TaskRabbit 排序场景，产品现在要把「客户手写的任务描述」和「tasker 上传的作品照片」也用进排序信号。
scenario_en: Same TaskRabbit ranking setup, but the product now wants the client's free-text job description and the tasker's uploaded photos to feed the ranking signal.
q: 加入自由文本和图片之后，模型该怎么调整？
q_en: Once free text and images enter the picture, how should the model change?
options: 把文本长度、有没有图片、图片张数这些统计量当成新的数值特征，继续沿用原来那套树模型
让标注同学把每条任务描述人工归到 20 个品类里，再当成类别特征喂给原来的树模型
用预训练模型把文本和图片编成 embedding 再喂排序模型，让表示学习接手
直接把原始文本字符串当成类别特征丢进 XGBoost，让它按字符串取值去做分裂就行
options_en: Turn text length, has-photo, and photo count into new numeric features and keep the same tree model.
Have annotators bucket each job description into 20 categories by hand and feed that as a categorical feature to the tree.
Encode text and images with pretrained models into embeddings, then feed the ranker — this is where representation learning pays off.
Drop the raw text string into XGBoost as a categorical feature and let it split on string values.
tradeoff: 树 + 统计量 vs 预训练 embedding：统计量便宜且当天就能上，代价是把「他到底想找人做什么」这层语义整个丢掉。
why: 非结构化输入正是深度学习的强项，而且有预训练模型可以直接编码，不必从零训练；这时候再用统计量近似就是在丢信息。
why_en: Unstructured input is exactly where deep learning wins, and pretrained encoders let you buy that representation instead of training one from scratch.
whenOtherWins: 如果文本又短又模板化（只有「组装 IKEA 书柜」这类固定说法），几个统计量加品类就够了，上 embedding 是过度设计。
optionMeanings: 用长度、张数等统计量替代内容。
靠人工标注把文本降维成品类。
用预训练编码器产出稠密向量。
把原始字符串当类别取值。
optionMeanings_en: Replace content with statistics like length and count.
Use human labeling to collapse text into categories.
Use pretrained encoders to produce dense vectors.
Treat the raw string as a categorical value.
optionDirectness: 文本短且格式固定时够用。
品类维度很小、标注量可控时可行。
内容语义本身携带排序信号时的做法。
取值稀疏到几乎每行一个类别，学不到东西。
optionDirectness_en: Enough when the text is short and templated.
Workable when categories are few and labeling volume is manageable.
The move when the semantics themselves carry ranking signal.
Values are so sparse that nearly every row is its own category, so nothing is learned.
optionScenarioImpacts: 「装书柜」和「修水管」被当成同一件事。
标注跟不上新任务类型的增长速度。
语义相近的任务和 tasker 能被匹配上。
树会在无穷多取值上疯狂分裂并过拟合。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: "Assemble a bookshelf" and "fix a pipe" look identical to the model.
Labeling can't keep up with new job types appearing.
Semantically similar jobs and taskers actually get matched.
The tree splits endlessly on unique values and overfits.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把文本或图片压成稠密向量，使语义相近的内容在向量空间里靠得近。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding compresses text or images into a dense vector so similar content lands nearby.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让模型自己从原始输入里学出有用的特征表示，而不是人工设计特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Representation learning lets the model derive useful features from raw input instead of hand-designing them.

q: XGBoost 与深度学习各自的主场，一句话怎么划？
q_en: In one line, how do you split the territory between XGBoost and deep learning?
text: XGBoost 赢在{{表格}}数据、缺失值原生处理和{{可解释}}性，中小样本（约百万行以内）训练一轮只要几分钟；深度学习赢在{{非结构化}}输入（文本、图像、音频）、超大数据集和有{{预训练}}模型可直接复用的场景。
text_en: XGBoost wins on {{tabular}} data, native missing-value handling and {{interpretability}}, training in minutes at small-to-medium scale; deep learning wins on {{unstructured}} input such as text, images and audio, on very large datasets, and when a {{pretrained}} model can be reused directly.
why: 面试里我上次只说了「结构化特征、数据不大、迭代快」——把可解释性和「深度学习什么时候反而赢」补上，答案才算有深度。
why_en: Last time I only said structured features, small data, fast iteration — adding interpretability and the cases where deep learning actually wins is what turns it into a real answer.

scenario: TaskRabbit ML 平台电话面：「如果你加入 TaskRabbit，你会怎么搭排序系统？」上次我讲完前两块就停了。
scenario_en: TaskRabbit ML platform screen: "If you joined TaskRabbit, how would you build the ranking system?" Last time I stopped after the first two pieces.
q: 把 ML 排序系统设计答案的五个模块排成正确顺序。
q_en: Put the five components of an ML ranking system answer in the right order.
steps: 在线服务：统计特征离线批算进 feature store，实时特征现查，卡住 100ms 延迟预算
候选召回：品类、距离、时段、预算做硬过滤，再用 ANN 把上万 tasker 砍到几百个
实验：A/B 切流量看 booking rate，同时盯住 tasker 供给健康度这条 guard metric
离线训练 pipeline：曝光日志 + 预订日志造标签，处理 position bias，用 AUC/NDCG 评估
排序模型：tasker 侧、客户侧、交叉特征，v1 预测 P(booking)
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["全部 tasker"] --> B["召回 硬过滤 加 ANN"]
  B --> C["排序模型 打分"]
  C --> D["返回 top-N 给客户"]
  D --> E["曝光与预订日志 回流训练"]
why: 五块的顺序就是数据流：先把候选缩小，再打分，再回头讲这个模型怎么训出来、怎么上线、怎么验证有效。
why_en: The five blocks follow the data flow: shrink the candidate set, score it, then explain how that model gets trained, served, and proven to work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻检索，用少量精度换极大的检索速度提升。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN stands for approximate nearest neighbor search, trading a little accuracy for a large speedup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一存放线上线下特征的服务，保证训练和推理用的是同一份特征定义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store holds features for both training and serving so the same definition is used in each.

termDefinitions.meaning: 展示位置靠前的条目天然更容易被点击，日志因此高估它们的质量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Position bias means items shown higher get clicked more, so logs overstate how good they are.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量模型把正样本排在负样本前面的整体能力，0.5 是瞎猜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC measures how well a model ranks positives above negatives, where 0.5 is random guessing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带位置折扣的排序质量指标，越靠前的相关结果加分越多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG scores ranking quality with a position discount, rewarding relevant results placed near the top.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实验里必须不能变坏的护栏指标，防止主指标涨了但生态被搞坏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guard metric is a guardrail that must not regress, protecting the ecosystem while the primary metric moves.

scenario: TaskRabbit 排序题：我讲完了候选召回和排序模型的特征，面试官点头说「继续」。上一次我就是在这里停住的。
scenario_en: TaskRabbit ranking question: I've covered candidate retrieval and the ranking model's features, and the interviewer nods and says "go on." Last time this is exactly where I stopped.
q: 接下来最该讲的是哪一块？
q_en: Which block should come next?
options: 继续往排序模型里加特征：再补上 tasker 的取消率、响应时长、品类历史表现和价格分位
跳到系统架构图：把网关、服务层、缓存和读写分离的数据库拓扑画出来
讲离线训练 pipeline：标签怎么定义、曝光与预订日志怎么造样本、离线用什么指标评估
先讲模型兜底：排序服务挂掉时退化成按评分排序的静态列表，保证页面不空
options_en: Keep adding features to the ranker: cancellation rate, response time, category history, price percentile.
Jump to the architecture diagram: gateway, service layer, cache, and a primary-replica database topology.
Cover the offline training pipeline: how labels are defined, how impression and booking logs build samples, and the offline metrics.
Cover the fallback first: if ranking dies, degrade to a static list sorted by rating so the page isn't empty.
tradeoff: 横向铺开五模块 vs 纵向深挖排序模型：铺开证明我懂完整 ML 系统，代价是每块只能给三十秒。
why: 召回和排序只是前两块；训练 pipeline、服务、实验这后三块才是区分「会调包」和「能上线」的地方，也正是我上次漏掉的。
why_en: Retrieval and ranking are only the first two blocks; the training pipeline, serving, and experimentation are what separate someone who calls a library from someone who ships, and they're exactly what I skipped.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确说「我只想听模型部分」，那就该往特征和目标函数里深挖，而不是横向铺开五个模块。
optionMeanings: 在同一块里继续堆特征。
切换成通用后端架构叙事。
进入第三块：数据与标签怎么来。
先补容灾降级方案。
optionMeanings_en: Keep piling features onto the same block.
Switch to a generic backend architecture narrative.
Move to block three: where data and labels come from.
Cover the degradation fallback first.
optionDirectness: 对方追问「特征还有哪些」时才合适。
题目本来问的是后端系统时才对题。
对方要看完整 ML 生命周期时的下一步。
面试后期讨论可靠性时再补更自然。
optionDirectness_en: Right only if they ask what other features exist.
On topic only if the question was a backend system.
The next step when they want the full ML lifecycle.
More natural later, when reliability comes up.
optionScenarioImpacts: 显得只会堆特征，看不到全景。
答成了通用后端题，ML 深度反而没了。
把答案推进到我上次漏掉的后三块。
重要但不紧急，会挤掉训练与实验的时间。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Reads as feature-piling with no view of the whole system.
Turns it into a generic backend answer and loses the ML depth.
Pushes into the three blocks I dropped last time.
Important but not urgent; it crowds out training and experimentation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把取数、造样本、训练、评估串起来的自动化流程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pipeline chains data extraction, sample building, training, and evaluation into one automated flow.

scenario: 排序模型的训练样本从曝光日志和预订日志拼出来：当时展示在第 1 位的 tasker 天然更容易被点、被预订。
scenario_en: Training samples are joined from impression and booking logs, and whoever sat in position one back then was naturally more likely to be clicked and booked.
q: 直接拿「被预订=1、未预订=0」训练会踩什么坑，怎么修？
q_en: What breaks if you train straight on booked=1 versus not-booked=0, and how do you fix it?
options: 只是正负样本不平衡：正样本太少，给正样本加权或做过采样，离线指标自然就上来了
没有坑，预订是真实转化信号，是这个业务里能拿到的最干净的 ground truth 标签
问题在标签延迟：客户下单后要几天才完成任务，训练时应该只把已完成且好评的订单算正样本
模型会把「排得靠前」学成「质量高」——位置当特征训练、推理时置零，或按位置做倾向加权
options_en: It's just class imbalance: too few positives, so weight or oversample them and the offline metric recovers.
No trap here; booking is a real conversion signal and the cleanest ground truth this business can get.
The issue is label delay: jobs complete days after booking, so only completed and well-rated jobs should count as positives.
The model learns "was ranked high" as "is high quality" — train position as a feature and zero it at inference, or reweight by position.
tradeoff: 位置特征置零 vs 倾向性加权：前者实现简单，代价是只能消掉线性的位置效应；后者更彻底但要估准倾向分。
why: 日志是旧模型自己造出来的，位置越靠前曝光越多，标签因此偏向旧模型的偏好；不纠偏就是让新模型抄旧模型的作业。
why_en: The logs were produced by the old ranker, so higher slots got more exposure and the labels inherit its preferences — without a debias step the new model just copies the old one.
whenOtherWins: 如果曝光是随机打散的（比如有一小片探索流量），位置效应本来就被随机化掉了，直接用日志标签是可以的。
optionMeanings: 把问题归为类别不平衡。
认为预订标签本身没有偏差。
把问题归为标签成熟得太晚。
识别出位置偏差并给出纠偏手段。
optionMeanings_en: Frames it as class imbalance.
Claims the booking label carries no bias.
Frames it as labels maturing too late.
Identifies position bias and gives a debias method.
optionDirectness: 正负比例极端时确实要处理，但不是本题的病根。
只有当曝光顺序随机时才成立。
当「预订后取消」很多时值得单独处理。
日志由旧排序模型生成时的必修课。
optionDirectness_en: Worth handling at extreme ratios, but it isn't the root cause here.
Only holds if the impression order was randomized.
Worth handling separately when post-booking cancellations are common.
Required whenever the logs were generated by a previous ranker.
optionScenarioImpacts: 指标好看了，模型照样把老的头部往前推。
新模型固化旧模型的偏好，长尾 tasker 永远起不来。
标签更干净，但位置带来的偏差原样保留。
模型学到的是真实质量，而不是当年的展示顺序。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The metric looks better while the model still pushes the same old head taskers up.
The new model freezes the old one's preferences and long-tail taskers never surface.
Labels get cleaner but the position-driven bias survives untouched.
The model learns actual quality instead of last year's display order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 展示位置靠前的条目天然更容易被点击，日志因此高估它们的质量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Position bias means items shown higher get clicked more, so the logs overstate how good they are.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被当作正确答案的那份标注或真实结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ground truth is the label or real outcome treated as the correct answer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按一条样本「本来有多大概率被看到」的倒数给它加权，抵消曝光不均。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Propensity weighting divides each sample by its probability of being seen, cancelling uneven exposure.

scenario: 排序服务端到端延迟预算 100ms。tasker 的历史评分、完成率每天批量算一次就够；「此刻是否有空」必须是当下的真值。
scenario_en: The ranking service has a 100ms end-to-end latency budget: historical rating and completion rate can be batch-computed daily, but "available right now" must be current.
q: 在线服务层该怎么切分这两类特征？
q_en: How should the serving layer split these two kinds of features?
options: 按新鲜度分层：统计类特征离线批算进 feature store，可用性现查，服务端只拼装
全部实时算：每次请求现场扫订单表算完成率和评分，保证所有特征都绝对新鲜、没有滞后
全部预计算：连「此刻是否有空」也每天跑一次批任务写进表，线上只做一次查表，最省延迟
把排序整体离线化：每晚为每个客户预生成一份 tasker 排名，白天的请求直接读缓存返回结果
options_en: Split by freshness: batch-compute statistical features into a feature store, look up availability at request time, and let the service just assemble them.
Compute everything live: scan the orders table on each request for completion rate and rating so nothing is ever stale.
Precompute everything, even "available now," in a nightly batch, so serving is a single table lookup and latency is minimal.
Move ranking fully offline: pregenerate a tasker ranking per client each night and serve it straight from cache during the day.
tradeoff: 分层特征 vs 全实时：分层把重计算挪到离线，代价是要保证离线和在线用的是同一份特征定义，否则训练与服务会不一致。
why: 特征该在线还是离线，取决于它的新鲜度要求而不是取决于口味；100ms 预算里塞不下扫全表，但也不能把「现在有没有空」缓存一天。
why_en: Whether a feature is computed online or offline is decided by how fresh it must be, not by taste: a full table scan won't fit in 100ms, but availability can't be a day old either.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有特征都必须秒级新鲜（比如竞价场景的实时预算余额），那就得整体走实时特征通路，并为此单独扩容。
optionMeanings: 按新鲜度要求把特征分成两条通路。
所有特征请求时现算。
所有特征都进夜间批任务。
把整个排序结果提前算好。
optionMeanings_en: Route features down two paths by freshness requirement.
Compute every feature at request time.
Push every feature into a nightly batch.
Precompute the entire ranking result.
optionDirectness: 同一模型里既有慢变量又有快变量时的标准切法。
特征全部秒级变化时才需要。
所有特征都是天级慢变量时才成立。
候选集小、个性化弱时可行。
optionDirectness_en: The standard split when one model mixes slow-moving and fast-moving signals.
Only needed when every feature changes by the second.
Only holds if every feature is a daily slow-moving value.
Workable when the candidate set is small and personalization is weak.
optionScenarioImpacts: 重计算搬去离线，100ms 预算留给拼装和打分。
扫订单表就吃掉了整个延迟预算。
会把已经接满单的 tasker 继续推给客户。
客户改一次筛选条件，缓存的排名就全失效。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Heavy computation moves offline and the 100ms budget goes to assembly and scoring.
Scanning the orders table alone eats the entire latency budget.
Fully booked taskers keep getting recommended to clients.
One filter change from the client invalidates the whole cached ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一存放线上线下特征的服务，保证训练和推理用同一份特征定义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store holds features for training and serving so both use the same definition.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个特征允许滞后多久还不影响决策质量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Feature freshness is how stale a feature may be before it stops being useful for the decision.

scenario: 白板上我要解耦「数据摄入」和「后续处理」。上一场我张口就说 Kafka，被追问「consumer group 是怎么工作的」时卡住了。
scenario_en: On the whiteboard I need to decouple ingestion from processing. Last time I opened with Kafka and froze when asked how consumer groups actually work.
q: 这次开口时该怎么选词？
q_en: How should I phrase it this time?
options: 还是先说 Kafka，它毕竟是行业标准；真被追问实现细节就坦白自己只在架构图上见过，没落过地
先说「用一个异步队列解耦摄入和处理」；只有当我能讲清分区与消费组这一层时，才主动点名 Kafka
说完 Kafka 立刻转移话题，赶紧往下画 worker pool 和数据库，不给面试官留出追问的空档
换成 RabbitMQ，它的模型更简单；被追问时解释 exchange 和 queue 比解释分区容易得多
options_en: Still open with Kafka since it's the industry standard, and if pressed on internals admit I've only seen it on architecture diagrams.
Say "an async queue decouples ingestion from processing" first, and only name Kafka once I can carry the partition and consumer-group layer.
Say Kafka then immediately move on to the worker pool and database, leaving no gap for a follow-up question.
Switch to RabbitMQ because its model is simpler and explaining exchanges and queues beats explaining partitions.
tradeoff: 点名 Kafka vs 只说异步队列：点名显得懂行，代价是把追问引到我讲不深的那一层。
why: 点名一个具体技术等于邀请对方往下追一层；讲不到 topic、消费组、并行度这一层就先用「异步队列」，被问到再升级。
why_en: Naming a specific technology invites the interviewer one level deeper, so I say "async queue" until I can actually carry topics, consumer groups, and parallelism.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方的技术栈页面上就写着 Kafka，或他自己先提了，那就直接用 Kafka 的词汇讲——这时候绕开反而显得生疏。
optionMeanings: 先点名具体技术，细节靠坦白兜底。
先给通用抽象，深度够了再点名。
点名后靠加快节奏躲开追问。
换一个自认为更好解释的中间件。
optionMeanings_en: Name the technology first and fall back on candor for details.
Give the generic abstraction first, name the tech only when depth allows.
Name it and outrun the follow-up by speeding up.
Swap in a middleware I think is easier to explain.
optionDirectness: 只有当岗位不要求这块深度时才无害。
当我对细节没把握、但架构判断正确时的稳妥选法。
赶时间时的下策，掩盖不了知识缺口。
只有当业务确实是任务分发而非日志流时才对。
optionDirectness_en: Harmless only if the role doesn't need that depth.
The safe choice when my architectural call is right but my details aren't.
A rushed fallback that doesn't hide the gap.
Right only if the workload is task dispatch rather than a log stream.
optionScenarioImpacts: 「只在架构图上见过」直接坐实经验不足。
判断照样得分，追问落在我能接住的层级。
面试官通常会绕回来，反而更尴尬。
换个名字，同样会被追问投递语义和顺序保证。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: "Only on diagrams" confirms the experience gap outright.
The architectural judgment still scores, and follow-ups land where I can answer.
The interviewer usually circles back, which is worse.
A different name, but they'll still ask about delivery semantics and ordering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个分布式日志型消息系统，消息按 topic 分区持久化，消费者按 offset 拉取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log-based messaging system where messages are persisted in partitioned topics and consumers pull by offset.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组共同消费某个 topic 的消费者，分区在组内被分配、互不重复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consumer group is a set of consumers sharing a topic, with each partition assigned to exactly one of them.

termDefinitions.meaning: RabbitMQ 里负责按路由规则把消息投进队列的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An exchange is the RabbitMQ component that routes messages into queues by rule.

scenario: 面试官追问：「你说的 Kafka，消费端具体是怎么并行的？投递语义是什么？」这就是必须能接住的那一层。
scenario_en: The follow-up: "With Kafka, how does the consumer side actually parallelize, and what are the delivery semantics?" This is the layer I must be able to carry.
q: Kafka 深一层的三句话分别是什么？
q_en: What are the three sentences one level below "we'd use Kafka"?
text: producer 发布到一个 {{topic}}；同一个 consumer group 内，每个 partition 只会被{{一个}} consumer 处理，所以 {{partition}} 数决定了这个组的最大并行度；默认投递是 {{at-least-once}}，因此消费端的处理必须幂等。
text_en: A producer publishes to a {{topic}}; within one consumer group each partition is handled by exactly {{one}} consumer, so the {{partition}} count caps that group's parallelism; delivery is {{at-least-once}} by default, so consumer-side processing must be idempotent.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  P["producer"] --> T["topic orders"]
  T --> P0["partition 0"]
  T --> P1["partition 1"]
  T --> P2["partition 2"]
  P0 --> C0["consumer A"]
  P1 --> C1["consumer B"]
  P2 --> C1
why: 这三句是 Kafka 的最小可辩护深度：消费者多过分区就有人闲着，扩并行必须先扩分区；重投是常态，所以幂等不是可选项。
why_en: These three sentences are the minimum defensible depth on Kafka: extra consumers sit idle beyond the partition count, and redelivery is normal so idempotency is not optional.

termDefinitions.meaning: topic 内的一条有序日志分片，是并行和顺序保证的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition is one ordered log shard inside a topic and the unit of both parallelism and ordering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 至少一次投递：不丢消息，但故障时同一条可能被重复投递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: At-least-once delivery never drops a message but may deliver the same one more than once after a failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一个操作重复执行多次，结果和执行一次相同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotent operation leaves the same result whether it runs once or many times.

scenario: 订单事件走 Kafka，消费端每收到一条就往结算表写一笔。某个 consumer 处理完、还没提交 offset 就崩了，rebalance 之后这条消息被重新投递。
scenario_en: Order events flow through Kafka and each one writes a settlement row. A consumer finishes processing, crashes before committing its offset, and after rebalance the message is redelivered.
q: 这条消息会怎样，消费端该怎么设计？
q_en: What happens to that message, and how should the consumer be designed?
options: Kafka 会检测到 offset 未提交并丢弃该消息，结算表不会重复，业务侧不用额外处理
把 offset 改成处理之前先提交，就变成至多一次，宁可漏也不重——结算场景这样最安全
开启 Kafka 事务把生产和消费包在一起，端到端恰好一次，业务侧就完全不用再管幂等了
消息会被重投、重复处理一次，所以写入要按事件唯一键做幂等——唯一索引或 upsert
options_en: Kafka detects the uncommitted offset and drops the message, so the settlement table never duplicates and no extra handling is needed.
Commit the offset before processing so it becomes at-most-once — better to lose one than to double-charge in settlement.
Turn on Kafka transactions to wrap produce and consume together for end-to-end exactly-once, so business code needn't be idempotent.
It gets redelivered and processed twice, so the write must be idempotent on an event key — unique index or upsert.
why: 崩溃发生在「已写库、未提交 offset」的中间态，Kafka 只能重投，无从知道你写没写；恢复的代价就是重复执行，只能靠消费端幂等收尾。
why_en: The crash lands between writing the row and committing the offset, and Kafka can only redeliver because it cannot know what you already wrote, so the recovery cost is duplicate work that only consumer-side idempotency absorbs.
optionMeanings: 认为 broker 能回滚未确认的处理。
把语义降级成至多一次。
认为事务能覆盖外部数据库写。
承认重复并用唯一键去重。
optionMeanings_en: Assumes the broker can roll back unacknowledged work.
Downgrades the semantics to at-most-once.
Assumes transactions cover an external database write.
Accepts duplication and dedupes on a unique key.
optionDirectness: broker 看不见消费端的副作用，做不到这件事。
只有当丢一条比重一条代价小时（如日志采样）才合理。
Kafka 事务只覆盖 Kafka 内部的读改写，不含外部库。
副作用写在外部存储时唯一可靠的做法。
optionDirectness_en: The broker cannot see consumer-side side effects, so it cannot do this.
Reasonable only when losing one costs less than repeating one, such as sampled logs.
Kafka transactions cover read-process-write inside Kafka, not an external store.
The only reliable move when side effects land in an external store.
optionScenarioImpacts: 结算表实际会多出一笔，账对不上。
崩溃时那笔订单永远不会结算，直接漏账。
结算库仍会写两次，事务保护不到它。
重投时 upsert 命中同一行，金额只算一次。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The settlement table really does gain an extra row and the books stop balancing.
That order is never settled after a crash — a silent miss.
The settlement database is still written twice; the transaction doesn't reach it.
On redelivery the upsert hits the same row and the amount counts once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费者在分区里读到哪一条的位置游标，提交后表示这条之前都算处理完。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offset is the cursor marking how far a consumer has read in a partition; committing it declares everything before it done.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费组成员变化时重新分配分区归属的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rebalance reassigns partitions across a consumer group when its membership changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存在就更新、不存在就插入的一次写操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An upsert updates the row if it exists and inserts it otherwise, in a single write.

termDefinitions.meaning: at-most-once：先确认再处理，不会重复但故障时会丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: At-most-once acknowledges before processing, so nothing repeats but failures lose messages.

scenario: Gamma 后端岗电话面：「讲讲你构建 RESTful API 的经验。」上次我答成了「我在前端对齐合约、校验输入、处理 loading 状态」——那是在消费 API。
scenario_en: Gamma backend screen: "Tell me about your experience building RESTful APIs." Last time I answered from the consumer side — aligning contracts, validating inputs, handling loading states.
q: 后端岗位期待的答案该从哪里起头？
q_en: Where should the answer start for a backend role?
options: 从我用过的框架起头：Go 的 gin、Python 的 FastAPI，讲路由注册、中间件和参数绑定怎么写
从性能数字起头：这个接口扛多少 QPS、加了几层缓存、把 P99 从多少压到了多少毫秒
从服务端合约起头：资源怎么建模成 URL、用哪些 HTTP 语义和状态码、错误 envelope 长什么样
从前后端协作起头：怎么跟前端约字段、怎么在联调阶段发现字段类型不一致并改回来
options_en: Start from the frameworks I've used — gin in Go, FastAPI in Python — covering routing, middleware, and request binding.
Start from performance numbers: the QPS this endpoint handles, how many cache layers, how far P99 dropped.
Start from the server-side contract: how resources map to URLs, which HTTP semantics and status codes, what the error envelope looks like.
Start from frontend collaboration: agreeing on fields and catching type mismatches during integration testing.
tradeoff: 服务端合约视角 vs 消费方视角：讲合约证明我能定义接口，代价是要现场撑得住状态码和幂等的追问。
why: 问后端工程师这道题问的是「你怎么定义接口」，不是「你怎么用接口」；从资源、语义、错误、幂等起头才对得上题。
why_en: Asked of a backend engineer this is a design question about how you define an interface, not how you consume one, so lead with resources, semantics, errors, and idempotency.
whenOtherWins: 如果岗位本来就是前端或 BFF（Backend For Frontend），从消费方视角讲合约对齐和错误处理反而是对题的。
optionMeanings: 以框架用法为主线。
以吞吐与延迟数字为主线。
以服务端接口合约为主线。
以跨端协作过程为主线。
optionMeanings_en: Organize around framework usage.
Organize around throughput and latency numbers.
Organize around the server-side interface contract.
Organize around cross-team collaboration.
optionDirectness: 对方明确问「你们用什么栈」时才对口。
题目问的是规模化经验时才合适。
问的是「你怎么设计接口」时的正解。
岗位偏全栈或联调协调时才有分量。
optionDirectness_en: On point only when they ask what stack you use.
Fits when the question is about operating at scale.
The right frame when they ask how you design an interface.
Carries weight only for full-stack or integration-heavy roles.
optionScenarioImpacts: 变成工具介绍，看不出设计判断。
跳过了设计层，对方会觉得答非所问。
第一句就落在后端设计层，追问也在我准备过的范围。
重演上次那次失误，继续像个 API 消费方。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It turns into a tool tour with no design judgment visible.
Skipping the design layer reads as answering a different question.
The first sentence lands on backend design and the follow-ups stay in prepared territory.
Repeats last time's mistake and still sounds like an API consumer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一的响应外壳结构，把错误码、消息、出错字段固定放在同样的位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An envelope is a fixed response wrapper that always puts the error code, message, and offending field in the same place.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专为某个前端定制的后端聚合层，负责裁剪和拼装下游数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A BFF is a backend layer tailored to one frontend that trims and assembles data from downstream services.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒查询数，衡量接口吞吐的常用单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS means queries per second, the usual unit for endpoint throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 99 分位延迟：100 次请求里最慢的那 1 次的耗时水平。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: P99 is the 99th-percentile latency, the level the slowest one request in a hundred reaches.

scenario: 后端岗被问「讲讲你怎么设计 RESTful API」，我需要一个能顺下来的五步骨架。
scenario_en: Asked as a backend engineer how I design RESTful APIs, I need a five-step skeleton I can walk straight through.
q: 把 RESTful API 设计答案的五步排成正确顺序。
q_en: Put the five steps of a RESTful API design answer in the right order.
steps: 幂等性：PUT/PATCH 天然幂等，POST 创建要靠客户端生成 ID 或幂等键才敢重试
资源建模：找出领域名词，映射成 /campaigns/{id} 这样的路径，所有权清晰才做嵌套
统一错误 envelope：固定 code、message、field 三段结构，绝不用 200 返回错误体
合约优先：先定 request/response schema 并和调用方对齐，破坏性变更走 /v1/ 路径版本
HTTP 语义与状态码：GET 读、POST 建返 201、PUT 全量替换、PATCH 局部改，配 400/404/422/500
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["资源建模 URL"] --> B["HTTP 语义与状态码"]
  B --> C["统一错误 envelope"]
  C --> D["幂等与安全重试"]
  D --> E["合约优先与版本化"]
why: 顺序是从名词到动词再到异常路径：先有资源，才谈用什么方法和状态码，再谈错怎么表达、重试怎么办，最后才是合约与版本。
why_en: The order runs from nouns to verbs to failure paths: resources first, then methods and status codes, then how errors are expressed and retries survive, and only then contracts and versioning.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 的局部更新方法，只提交要改的字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PATCH is the HTTP method for a partial update that submits only the fields being changed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求和响应的字段结构与类型定义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A schema is the field structure and types defined for a request and response.

scenario: 创建 campaign 的接口收到一个 JSON 格式合法、但业务上无效的 body：budget_cap 是负数。前端要求能定位到是哪个字段错了。
scenario_en: The create-campaign endpoint receives a syntactically valid JSON body that is semantically invalid: budget_cap is negative. The frontend needs to know which field failed.
q: 该返回什么状态码、什么响应体？
q_en: What status code and response body should come back?
options: 返回 400 或 422，body 用固定 envelope 带上 code、message 和出错的 field
返回 200，body 里带 success=false 和一段 msg，让前端统一只看 success 这个字段来判断
返回 500，服务端确实没能完成创建；细节写进日志，响应体只给一个 trace id 让后端去查
返回 404，表示这个 budget_cap 取值对应的资源不存在，让前端提示用户换一个取值再试
options_en: Return 400 or 422 with a fixed envelope carrying code, message, and the offending field.
Return 200 with success=false and a msg string, so the frontend only ever checks the success flag.
Return 500 since the server did fail to create it; log the details and return only a trace id for the backend to look up.
Return 404 meaning no resource matches that budget_cap value, and let the frontend ask the user for another value.
tradeoff: 400 vs 422：400 表示请求本身有问题、通用且到处支持，422 更精确地表达「语法没错但语义不通过」，团队内统一一种即可。
why: 错在调用方的输入，属于 4xx；用状态码表达类别、用 envelope 表达细节，前端才能既做通用处理又能定位字段。
why_en: The caller's input is wrong so it belongs in the 4xx family, with the status code carrying the category and the envelope carrying the field-level detail.

scenario: 创建 campaign 的 POST 请求，客户端在超时后自动重试。上下游对齐的超时是 1000ms，重试很可能发生在服务端已经写库之后。
scenario_en: A create-campaign POST is auto-retried by the client after a timeout. The agreed upstream timeout is 1000ms, so the retry may fire after the server already committed the write.
q: 怎么保证重试不会创建出两条 campaign？
q_en: How do you keep the retry from creating two campaigns?
options: 先 GET 查一遍再决定要不要 POST：查不到就创建、查到了就返回已有那条，靠读来避免重复
在服务端加一层五秒内相同 body 去重的内存缓存，重复请求直接返回上一次的结果
让客户端别自动重试：超时就把错误抛给用户，由用户自己决定要不要再点一次提交
带 Idempotency-Key 请求头：服务端按 key 存首次结果，重试时直接回放
options_en: GET first and decide whether to POST: create if absent, return the existing one if present, using a read to avoid duplicates.
Add a server-side in-memory cache that dedupes identical bodies within five seconds and replays the previous result.
Stop the client from auto-retrying: surface the timeout to the user and let them decide whether to submit again.
Send an Idempotency-Key header: the server stores the first result under that key and replays it for any retry with the same key.
tradeoff: 幂等键 vs 先查后写：幂等键在服务端一次性定生死，代价是要存一张 key→结果的表并给它定 TTL；先查后写不用存表，但挡不住并发。
why: POST 创建天然不幂等，重试必须靠一个由客户端生成的稳定 key 把「同一次意图」认出来；先查后写在并发下有检查与写入之间的竞态。
why_en: POST creation is not idempotent by nature, so a stable client-generated key is what lets the server recognize the same intent, while check-then-write leaves a race between the read and the write.
whenOtherWins: 如果这个写操作本身就是 PUT 全量替换或 DELETE，方法语义已经保证重试安全，不需要再引入额外的幂等键。
codeSample:
POST /v1/campaigns HTTP/1.1
Idempotency-Key: 7d3f9c2a-5b41-4e88-9f10-2c6a1b8e4d55
Content-Type: application/json

{ "shop_id": "s_1024", "budget_cap": 500 }

termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotency key is a client-generated request identifier the server uses to recognize a retry of the same intent.

scenario: Anytime AI 法律 RAG 轮：面试官问「你们向量库用什么索引？HNSW 是怎么工作的？」上一次我直接坦白说不熟。
scenario_en: Anytime AI legal-RAG round: "What index does your vector store use, and how does HNSW work?" Last time I simply admitted I wasn't familiar with it.
q: 一句话说清 HNSW 的结构，以及它为什么快？
q_en: In one sentence, what is HNSW's structure and why is it fast?
options: 它把向量聚成若干簇、记住每个簇的中心点，查询时只扫离问题最近的几个簇——即倒排文件索引
它是一张分层的邻近图：上层稀疏用来长距离跳跃，逐层下沉到底层做精搜，复杂度接近对数
它用多组随机哈希函数把相近的向量映到同一个桶里，查询时只比较同一个桶内的向量
它按维度轮流二分建一棵平衡树，查询时沿树下降并回溯，在高维下依然保持对数复杂度
options_en: It clusters vectors, remembers each cluster centroid, and scans only the nearest few clusters — that's an inverted file index.
It's a layered proximity graph: sparse upper layers make long jumps, then it descends layer by layer to a fine search, at near-logarithmic cost.
It hashes nearby vectors into the same bucket with several random hash functions and compares only within a bucket.
It bisects on one dimension at a time to build a balanced tree, descending and backtracking, staying logarithmic even in high dimensions.
tradeoff: HNSW vs 暴力精确扫描：HNSW 用内存和建图时间换近似对数的查询延迟，代价是召回不再是 100%，还多了一组参数要调。
why: HNSW 是分层可导航小世界图：节点随机分配最高层数，上层长边负责快速逼近，底层短边负责精确收敛，所以查询近似对数复杂度。
why_en: HNSW is a hierarchical navigable small-world graph where upper-layer long edges get you close fast and bottom-layer short edges converge precisely, giving near-logarithmic search.
whenOtherWins: 如果向量只有几万条，或者内存吃紧、写入极其频繁，暴力精确扫描或 IVF 更省内存，也不必调图参数。
diagram:
flowchart TD
  L2["上层 稀疏图 长距离跳跃"] --> L1["中层 逐步逼近"]
  L1 --> L0["底层 含全部向量 精搜"]
  L0 --> R["返回 top-k 近邻"]
optionMeanings: 聚类分桶再扫最近的簇。
分层图上从粗到细导航。
用局部敏感哈希分桶。
按维度递归二分建树。
optionMeanings_en: Cluster into buckets and scan the nearest ones.
Navigate a layered graph from coarse to fine.
Bucket by locality-sensitive hashing.
Recursively bisect by dimension into a tree.
optionDirectness: 这是 IVF 的做法，内存省但召回更依赖分簇质量。
正是 HNSW 的结构，也是它对数复杂度的来源。
这是 LSH，实现简单但同精度下要更多桶和更多比较。
这是 KD-tree，维度一高就退化成接近全扫。
optionDirectness_en: That's IVF: cheaper on memory but recall depends heavily on clustering quality.
That is HNSW's structure and the source of its logarithmic cost.
That's LSH: simple to build but needs more buckets and comparisons for the same precision.
That's a KD-tree, which degrades to nearly a full scan in high dimensions.

接得住「怎么调召回」这个必然的下一问。
把哈希方案说成图结构，术语一混就露怯。
在几百上千维的文本向量上根本立不住。

It sets up the inevitable next question about tuning recall.
Calling a hashing scheme a graph mixes up the vocabulary and shows.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分层可导航小世界图：一种多层邻近图的近似最近邻索引，查询近似对数复杂度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HNSW stands for hierarchical navigable small world, a multi-layer proximity graph index for approximate nearest neighbor search with near-logarithmic query cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻检索，用一点精度换极大的速度提升。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN stands for approximate nearest neighbor search, trading a bit of accuracy for a large speedup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 倒排文件索引：先把向量聚类，查询时只扫最近的若干个簇。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IVF stands for inverted file: vectors are clustered first and a query scans only the nearest clusters.

termDefinitions.meaning: 局部敏感哈希：让相近的向量大概率落进同一个哈希桶。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LSH stands for locality-sensitive hashing, which makes nearby vectors likely to land in the same bucket.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按维度轮流切分空间的树形索引，维度一高效率急剧下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A KD-tree splits space one dimension at a time and degrades sharply as dimensionality grows.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把文本压成稠密向量，使语义相近的文本在向量空间里靠得近。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding turns text into a dense vector so semantically similar text lands nearby.

scenario: 法律 RAG 上线后抽查发现：有些明确写在文档里的条款没被检索到。当前 p99 检索延迟 20ms，预算是 80ms。
scenario_en: After launch, spot checks show the legal RAG misses clauses that are plainly in the documents. Retrieval p99 is 20ms today against an 80ms budget.
q: 第一个该动的旋钮是什么？
q_en: Which knob do you turn first?
options: 把 chunk 切得更小：块越小语义越集中，同样的 top-k 就能覆盖到更多条款文本
换一个维度更高的 embedding 模型：语义表达更细，重新灌一遍库，漏检自然会减少
把 top-k 从 5 调到 50：一次多返回一些块，让模型自己在长上下文里挑相关的
调大查询期的 ef_search：多探几个候选换更高召回，延迟会涨但预算还有余量
options_en: Cut chunks smaller: tighter chunks mean the same top-k covers more clause text.
Swap in a higher-dimensional embedding model, reindex everything, and misses drop naturally.
Raise top-k from 5 to 50 so more chunks come back and the model picks the relevant ones from a long context.
Raise ef_search at query time: explore more candidates for higher recall, with latency rising into the spare budget.
tradeoff: ef_search 调大 vs 调小：调大换召回，代价是每次查询要在图上多走一些节点、延迟大致线性上涨。
why: 漏的是索引层的近似误差，不是语义问题；ef_search 是查询期唯一的召回与延迟旋钮，而且改它不用重建索引、当天就能验证。
why_en: The misses come from approximation in the index rather than from semantics, and ef_search is the one query-time knob trading recall against latency without a reindex.
whenOtherWins: 如果 p99 已经贴着 80ms 预算，就不能再加 ef_search，该转向混合检索或加一层重排来提召回。
optionMeanings: 改切块粒度。
换更强的向量模型。
一次多取一些候选块。
调大查询期的候选探索列表。
optionMeanings_en: Change the chunking granularity.
Swap in a stronger embedding model.
Fetch more candidate chunks per query.
Widen the query-time candidate list.

当同义改写都检索不到、说明语义确实没编码好时才值。
当上下文预算充足、且后面有重排兜底时可行。
当漏检来自索引近似、且延迟预算还有余量时的首选。

Worth it only when paraphrases also fail, showing semantics really weren't captured.
Workable when context budget is ample and a reranker follows.
The first choice when misses come from index approximation and latency budget remains.

换模型要重灌全库，成本和周期都最大。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: ef_search is the size of the candidate list HNSW keeps during a query; larger means more nodes explored, higher recall, and more latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次检索返回最相似的前 k 个结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Top-k means returning the k most similar results from one retrieval.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把长文档切成的一小段，是向量化和检索的最小单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A chunk is a small slice of a long document and the unit that gets embedded and retrieved.

termDefinitions.meaning: 该被找回的相关内容里，实际被找回的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall is the share of the relevant items that retrieval actually returned.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding is the dense vector representation of a piece of text.

scenario: 律师搜「Section 12(b)(6) 动议」和具体案号，纯向量检索经常返回语义相近、但案号完全不对的段落。
scenario_en: Lawyers search for a Section 12(b)(6) motion and specific docket numbers, and pure vector retrieval keeps returning semantically similar passages with the wrong numbers.
q: 怎么把这类精确匹配救回来？
q_en: How do you recover this kind of exact matching?
options: 在 prompt 里加一句「必须严格匹配案号」，让模型自己在返回的块里筛掉不对的那些
做混合检索：向量召回加 BM25 关键词召回，两份排名用 RRF 融合成一个列表
把 embedding 模型换成在法律语料上微调过的版本，让它学会区分不同的案号数字
把 chunk 的重叠从 50 token 提到 200 token，让案号和它的上下文更容易落在同一块里
options_en: Add "the docket number must match exactly" to the prompt and let the model filter the wrong chunks itself.
Go hybrid: vector retrieval plus BM25 keyword retrieval, fusing the two rankings with RRF into one list.
Fine-tune the embedding model on legal text so it learns to tell different docket numbers apart.
Raise chunk overlap from 50 to 200 tokens so a docket number and its context land in the same chunk.
tradeoff: 混合检索 vs 纯向量：混合把罕见词和编号精确捞回来，代价是要多维护一套倒排索引和一个融合参数。
why: 稠密向量会把案号这类罕见 token 抹平，稀疏检索按词频精确命中；RRF 按名次融合，绕开两种分数量纲不可比的问题。
why_en: Dense vectors smear rare tokens like docket numbers while sparse retrieval matches them exactly, and rank-based fusion sidesteps the fact that the two score scales aren't comparable.
whenOtherWins: 如果查询几乎都是自然语言描述、极少出现编号或专有名词，加一路关键词检索只会增加运维负担而看不到收益。

在领域语料上微调向量模型。
加大切块重叠保住上下文。
optionMeanings_en: Push the filtering job onto the generation model.
Run sparse and dense retrieval, then fuse by rank.
Fine-tune the embedding model on domain text.
Increase chunk overlap to preserve context.

查询里同时有语义意图和必须精确命中的编号时的做法。
当同义表述都检索不到、说明领域语义没学会时才值。
当一个概念被切块切断时才对症。

The move when a query mixes semantic intent with tokens that must match exactly.
Worth it when even paraphrases fail, showing the domain semantics weren't learned.
On target only when chunking cut a single concept in half.

关键词那一路把带准确案号的段落直接顶上来。
微调周期以周计，救不了这周的线上漏检。
块变大更容易撑长上下文，编号仍可能没被召回。

The keyword leg pushes the passage with the exact docket number straight to the top.
Fine-tuning takes weeks and does nothing for this week's misses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 经典的关键词检索打分函数，按词频和文档长度给精确词匹配打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BM25 is a classic keyword scoring function that ranks exact term matches by term frequency and document length.

termDefinitions.meaning: 倒数排名融合：按每份列表里的名次倒数相加合并结果，不看原始分数量纲。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RRF stands for reciprocal rank fusion, merging lists by summing the reciprocal of each item's rank so incompatible score scales don't matter.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时跑关键词检索和向量检索，再把两份结果合成一份排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hybrid search runs keyword and vector retrieval together and merges the two result lists into one ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把文本压成稠密向量的表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding is the dense vector representation of a piece of text.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型切分文本的最小单位，英文里大约 4 个字符算一个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token is the smallest unit a model splits text into, roughly four characters of English.

scenario: 团队已经在跑 Postgres，法律文档预计几百万个 chunk，后端只有两个人、没有专职 SRE，还要按客户做关系型联表。
scenario_en: The team already runs Postgres, expects a few million document chunks, has two backend engineers and no dedicated SRE, and needs relational joins by customer.
q: 向量该存在哪里？
q_en: Where should the vectors live?
options: 上 Pinecone：全托管、零运维，把向量完全交出去，团队一行基础设施代码都不用写，按量付费
自建 Weaviate 集群：内置混合检索和多模态模块，功能最全，用 Kubernetes 跑起来
用 pgvector：向量和业务数据同库，省掉一整个服务和同步链路，百万级配 HNSW 够用
先用进程内的 FAISS 索引：启动时全量加载进内存，查询最快，重启时再重新建一遍
options_en: Go Pinecone: fully managed, zero ops, hand the vectors off entirely, no infrastructure code, pay per usage.
Self-host a Weaviate cluster: built-in hybrid and multimodal modules, the richest feature set, running on Kubernetes.
Use pgvector: vectors sit beside business data, no extra service or sync path, and HNSW is enough at a few million rows.
Start with an in-process FAISS index loaded fully into memory at boot, fastest queries, rebuilt on every restart.
tradeoff: pgvector vs 专用向量库：pgvector 省掉一整个服务和一条同步链路、还能和业务表联表，代价是上到几千万向量后调优空间不如专用库。
why: 两个人、没有 SRE、还要联表，决定性约束是运维面而不是极限性能；几百万 chunk 在 pgvector 加 HNSW 的舒适区里。
why_en: With two engineers, no SRE, and a need for joins, the deciding constraint is operational surface rather than peak performance, and a few million chunks sit well inside pgvector's comfort zone.
whenOtherWins: 如果向量涨到上亿、检索 QPS 很高、或者需要多模态与内置混合检索，专用向量库的调优空间和横向分片才值回那套运维成本。
optionMeanings: 把向量托管给外部服务。
自建功能最全的向量数据库。
在现有 Postgres 上加向量列和索引。
把索引放在应用进程内存里。
optionMeanings_en: Hand vectors to a managed external service.
Self-host the most feature-complete vector database.
Add a vector column and index to the existing Postgres.
Keep the index in the application process's memory.
optionDirectness: 团队完全不想碰基础设施、且不需要联表时合适。
需要多模态或内置混合检索、且有 K8s 能力时才划算。
已有 Postgres、要联表、规模在千万级以内时的默认解。
数据集小且只读、可以接受重启重建时的原型做法。
optionDirectness_en: Fits a team that refuses to touch infrastructure and needs no joins.
Pays off when you need multimodal or built-in hybrid search and have Kubernetes skills.
The default when Postgres already exists, joins matter, and scale stays under tens of millions.
A prototype move for a small read-only set where rebuilding on restart is acceptable.
optionScenarioImpacts: 多一套外部依赖和一条向量与业务数据的同步链路。
两个人还要养 K8s 集群，运维直接压垮迭代。
一条 SQL 就能带上租户过滤和业务字段联表。
重启期间检索不可用，也没法做持久化过滤。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You add an external dependency plus a sync path between vectors and business data.
Two engineers babysitting a Kubernetes cluster crushes iteration speed.
One SQL statement carries tenant filtering and joins to business columns.
Retrieval is unavailable during restarts and durable filtering isn't possible.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给 PostgreSQL 加向量列类型和近似最近邻索引的扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: pgvector is a PostgreSQL extension adding a vector column type and approximate nearest neighbor indexes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分层可导航小世界图，主流的近似最近邻索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HNSW stands for hierarchical navigable small world, the mainstream graph index for approximate nearest neighbor search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 站点可靠性工程师，专职负责线上系统的稳定与运维。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SRE stands for site reliability engineer, the role that owns production stability and operations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个进程内的向量相似度检索库，没有独立的服务与持久化层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FAISS is an in-process vector similarity search library with no standalone service or storage layer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 容器编排系统，负责调度、扩缩和自愈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kubernetes is a container orchestration system handling scheduling, scaling, and self-healing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一串浮点数，用来表示一段文本或图片的语义位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vector is a list of floating-point numbers representing where a piece of text or an image sits semantically.

scenario: 法律平台是多租户的：卖家 A 的问题绝不能检索到卖家 B 的文档。所有租户的 chunk 共用同一个向量索引。
scenario_en: The legal platform is multi-tenant: seller A's question must never retrieve seller B's documents, and every tenant's chunks share one vector index.
q: 租户隔离该在检索的哪一步实现？
q_en: At which step of retrieval should tenant isolation happen?
options: 先按向量取 top-50，再在应用层把不属于该租户的块丢掉，剩下多少用多少，实现最简单
给每个租户单独建一个索引，几万个租户就几万个索引，彻底物理隔离，互相之间不会串数据
在 prompt 里写明「只使用属于当前租户的材料」，让模型自己识别并忽略别人的文档
把 tenant_id 存进 chunk 的元数据，检索时带上过滤条件一起生效
options_en: Take the vector top-50 first, then drop non-tenant chunks in the application layer and use whatever remains — simplest to build.
Build one index per tenant: tens of thousands of tenants means tens of thousands of indexes, physically isolated with no crossover.
Write "use only the current tenant's materials" into the prompt and let the model recognize and ignore other documents.
Store tenant_id in the chunk metadata and pass a filter that applies during retrieval itself.
tradeoff: 共享索引加元数据过滤 vs 一租户一索引：共享省资源、扩容简单，代价是过滤选择性很低时图上要走更远才凑够候选。
why: 过滤必须发生在检索内部；事后剔除会让 top-k 名额先被别人的文档占满，真正相关的块根本没机会进候选集。
why_en: Filtering has to happen inside retrieval, because filtering afterwards lets other tenants' documents consume the top-k slots before the relevant chunks ever get a chance.
whenOtherWins: 如果租户只有十几个、每个数据量都很大，一租户一索引反而更简单，还能按各自的数据规模单独调参。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Q["问题向量"] --> F["带 tenant_id 过滤的检索"]
  F --> K["top-k 全部属于本租户"]
  Q --> N["无过滤检索"]
  N --> M["top-50 混入他人文档"]
  M --> X["应用层剔除后候选不足"]
optionMeanings: 先检索后在应用层剔除。
每个租户一套物理隔离的索引。
靠提示词约束模型自觉。
把租户号做成元数据并在检索时过滤。
optionMeanings_en: Retrieve first, then strip in the application layer.
One physically isolated index per tenant.
Rely on the prompt to keep the model honest.
Make tenant id metadata and filter during retrieval.
optionDirectness: 只有当同租户内容本来就占绝大多数时才勉强够。
租户数很少、单租户数据量大时反而更简单。
隔离是安全边界，不能交给概率性的模型判断。
共享索引下保证候选集全部合规的做法。
optionDirectness_en: Barely enough only when one tenant already dominates the corpus.
Simpler when tenants are few and each holds a lot of data.
Isolation is a security boundary and cannot rest on a probabilistic model.
The way to guarantee a compliant candidate set on a shared index.
optionScenarioImpacts: 小租户的文档永远挤不进 top-50，等于检索失灵。
几万个索引的创建、扩容和备份都要自己管。
一旦模型没照做就是跨租户数据泄漏事故。
候选集从一开始就只含本租户，也不浪费名额。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A small tenant's documents never reach the top-50, so retrieval effectively fails for them.
You now manage creation, scaling, and backup for tens of thousands of indexes.
One instance of the model not complying is a cross-tenant data leak.
The candidate set contains only this tenant from the start and no slots are wasted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给每个向量附带结构化字段，检索时按这些字段先限定搜索范围。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Metadata filtering attaches structured fields to each vector and restricts the search to matching ones.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一套系统同时服务多个互不可见的客户，数据必须严格隔离。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multi-tenancy means one system serves many customers who must never see each other's data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次检索返回最相似的前 k 个结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Top-k means returning the k most similar results from one retrieval.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一串浮点数，表示一段文本的语义位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vector is a list of floating-point numbers marking where text sits semantically.

scenario: Amazon Round 1 面试官追问「这些字段喂给 LLM，token size 大概多少？」我当场没有任何数字，承认从没查过。
scenario_en: In Amazon Round 1 the interviewer asked how many tokens those form fields become, and I had no number at all and admitted I'd never checked.
q: 字段到 token 的粗略换算该怎么当场算出来？
q_en: How do you estimate fields-to-tokens on the spot?
text: 英文经验值：1 token ≈ {{4}} 个字符 ≈ 0.75 个单词，也就是 100 token ≈ {{75}} 个单词；中文和代码同样长度会更费 token。一个 50–100 词的用户问题只有 70–130 token，真正把 context 撑大的是 {{prompt 模板}}和检索进来的上下文。
text_en: English rule of thumb: 1 token is about {{4}} characters or 0.75 words, so 100 tokens is roughly {{75}} words; Chinese and code cost more tokens for the same length. A 50-100 word user question is only 70-130 tokens, and what really inflates context is the {{prompt template}} plus the retrieved context.
why: 这个换算的用处是当场把「多加 5 个字段」翻译成「多几百 token」，再乘上单价和延迟曲线估出增量，而不是空着手被追问。
why_en: The point of the conversion is to turn "five more fields" into "a few hundred more tokens" on the spot, and then into a latency and cost delta instead of standing there with no number.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型切分文本的最小单位，英文里大约 4 个字符算一个 token。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token is the smallest unit a model splits text into, about four characters of English.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次请求里模型能看到的 token 总量上限，prompt 加输出都算在内。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The context window is the total token budget a model can see in one request, counting both prompt and output.

termDefinitions.meaning: 包在用户输入外面的固定指令、角色说明和格式要求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A prompt template is the fixed instructions, role description, and formatting rules wrapped around the user's input.

scenario: Amazon Round 1：我讲 Meta onboarding 砍字段的故事，面试官追问「这些字段是喂给 LLM 做推理的，加字段会怎么影响推理？」
scenario_en: Amazon Round 1: while telling the Meta onboarding story about cutting fields, the interviewer asked how adding more fields would affect the LLM inference they feed.
q: 该说出哪三个后果？
q_en: Which three consequences should I name?
options: 延迟随输入 token 增长、单次请求成本上升、相关信息被稀释导致 grounding 变差
准确率会随字段数单调上升，唯一代价是账单变贵，所以这纯粹是个成本问题而非质量问题
没有影响，只要没超过模型的 context window 上限，多少 token 对推理质量都是一样的
主要影响在训练侧：字段变多意味着要重新微调模型，推理侧本身几乎不受这个改动影响
options_en: Latency grows with input tokens, per-request cost rises, and the relevant signal gets diluted so grounding degrades.
Accuracy rises monotonically with field count and the only cost is a bigger bill, so this is purely a cost question.
No impact: as long as you stay under the context window limit, token count doesn't change inference quality.
The impact is on training: more fields means refitting the model, while inference itself is barely affected.
tradeoff: 多塞字段 vs 精选字段：多塞看着信息全，代价是延迟、成本和「中间被忽略」三重叠加。
why: 上下文不是免费的：token 变多推高延迟和单次成本，还会把关键事实稀释到模型不容易用上的位置，所以要问边际信息值不值这些 token。
why_en: Context isn't free — more tokens raise latency and per-request cost and dilute the key facts, so the real question is whether a field's marginal information is worth its token cost.
whenOtherWins: 如果模型本来就缺关键事实、答案频繁编造，那先把缺的字段补进去比省 token 重要得多。
optionMeanings: 延迟、成本、相关性稀释三条一起说。
认为信息越多质量单调上升。
认为窗口以内 token 数无关紧要。
把影响错误地归到训练侧。
optionMeanings_en: Names latency, cost, and dilution together.
Claims more information always means better quality.
Claims token count is irrelevant below the window limit.
Misplaces the impact onto the training side.
optionDirectness: 对方在 LLM 团队、要听工程成本时的完整答案。
当字段全是高价值事实、且模型有富余能力时才近似成立。
只有在 prompt 极短、远低于窗口时差异才可忽略。
只有当这些字段确实进了训练集时才相关。
optionDirectness_en: The complete answer when an LLM org wants the engineering cost.
Roughly true only when every field is high-value and the model has headroom.
The difference is negligible only for very short prompts far below the window.
Relevant only if those fields actually entered the training set.
optionScenarioImpacts: 把产品决定接回到延迟和成本上，正是这个组关心的。
忽略了长上下文会稀释信号，结论会偏向「多多益善」。
等于说加多少字段都无所谓，产品取舍无从谈起。
答偏到训练，面试官问的推理成本一句没答到。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It ties a product decision back to latency and cost, which is what this org cares about.
It ignores dilution in long contexts and drifts toward "more is always better."
It implies field count never matters, so no product tradeoff can be discussed.
It drifts to training and never answers the inference cost that was asked.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让模型的回答有据可依：答案必须建立在提供的上下文事实上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Grounding means the model's answer must be built on the facts supplied in its context.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次请求里模型能看到的 token 总量上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The context window is the maximum number of tokens a model can see in one request.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型切分文本的最小单位，英文里约 4 个字符一个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token is the smallest text unit for a model, about four English characters.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在预训练模型上用领域数据继续训练，改变模型权重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fine-tuning continues training a pretrained model on domain data, changing its weights.

scenario: grounding 上下文里拼了 20 段材料，关键那一段正好排在正中间。检索日志显示它确实被召回了，模型却答错了。
scenario_en: Twenty passages were packed into the grounding context and the key one sits right in the middle; retrieval logs confirm it was returned, yet the model still answered wrong.
q: 这最可能是什么现象，该怎么缓解？
q_en: What phenomenon is this most likely, and how do you mitigate it?
options: 是 embedding 模型不够好：关键段的向量表示不准，应该换一个更强的检索模型重新灌库
是 lost in the middle：模型对上下文首尾的信息用得最好，正中间那段最容易被忽略
是 tokenizer 把中间那段截断了：超出 context window 的部分被静默丢弃，模型根本没看到
是采样温度太高导致输出随机：把 temperature 调到 0，同样的上下文就能稳定答对了
options_en: The embedding model is too weak: the key passage's vector is off, so swap in a stronger retriever and reindex.
It's lost in the middle: models use information at the start and end of a context best and most easily overlook the middle.
The tokenizer truncated that passage: anything past the context window is silently dropped, so the model never saw it.
Sampling temperature is too high: set temperature to 0 and the same context will answer correctly every time.
why: 研究发现模型在长上下文上的准确率呈 U 形——信息在开头或结尾时最好、在中间时最差；缓解是重排后把最相关的放首尾，并压掉无关段。
why_en: Research shows accuracy over long contexts follows a U shape, best at the start and end and worst in the middle, so rerank the most relevant passage to an edge and drop the filler.
optionMeanings: 归因为检索质量问题。
归因为长上下文的位置效应。
归因为超窗被截断。
归因为解码随机性。
optionMeanings_en: Blames retrieval quality.
Blames the positional effect in long contexts.
Blames truncation past the window.
Blames decoding randomness.
optionDirectness: 当关键段根本没被召回时才是这个原因。
当日志显示已召回、位置又在中段时的典型解释。
当总 token 确实超过窗口上限时才成立。
当同一份输入多次运行结果不稳定时才是它。
optionDirectness_en: The right cause only when the key passage was never retrieved.
The typical explanation when logs show it was retrieved and it sits mid-context.
Holds only if total tokens really exceeded the window.
That's the cause only when repeated runs on the same input disagree.
optionScenarioImpacts: 重灌一次全库，位置效应原封不动，问题照旧。
改成重排加裁剪，关键段被顶到首尾，答案就稳了。
去查窗口用量会发现远没超，排查方向白走一趟。
温度归零只是让错误答案变得更稳定地错。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You reindex everything, the positional effect survives, and the bug remains.
Reranking and trimming push the key passage to an edge and the answer stabilizes.
Checking window usage shows you're nowhere near the limit — a wasted investigation.
Zero temperature just makes the wrong answer wrong more consistently.

termDefinitions.meaning: 长上下文里位于中段的信息最容易被模型忽略，准确率随位置呈 U 形。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lost in the middle describes how models most easily overlook information placed mid-context, with accuracy forming a U shape by position.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把文本切成 token 的组件，决定同一段话占多少 token。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tokenizer splits text into tokens and decides how many tokens a passage costs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 采样温度，控制生成的随机性，0 表示每次都取最高概率的词。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Temperature controls sampling randomness, where zero always picks the highest-probability token.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把文本压成稠密向量的表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding is the dense vector representation of text.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对检索回来的候选再打一次分，把最相关的顶到最前面。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reranking rescores the retrieved candidates so the most relevant ones move to the top.

scenario: 我在 Meta 砍掉了 onboarding 里的低价值字段，AI agent 的回答质量没有下降。面试官问：「输入信息变少了，凭什么质量不掉？」
scenario_en: I removed low-value onboarding fields at Meta and the AI agent's answer quality held. The interviewer asked why quality didn't drop when the input shrank.
q: 该怎么解释这件事？
q_en: How should I explain that?
options: 因为我们同时换了更强的基础模型，模型能力的提升刚好抵消了输入信息量的减少
因为 A/B 测试的 treatment 组质量没有显著回归，既然指标没动，说明砍字段本来就无所谓
因为剩下的字段做了摘要压缩，总信息量其实没变，只是换成了一种更省 token 的表达方式
被砍的字段多半是空值或默认值；context 更短更干净，grounding 看的是质量不是字段数
options_en: We swapped in a stronger base model at the same time, and the capability gain offset the lost input.
The A/B treatment showed no significant regression, and since the metric didn't move, cutting fields never mattered.
The remaining fields were summarized, so total information is unchanged — just expressed in fewer tokens.
The removed fields were mostly empty or default; a shorter, cleaner context still grounds well because quality beats field count.
tradeoff: 减字段 vs 保全量：减字段换来更短更干净的上下文和更低的填写摩擦，代价是必须先拿实验证明质量没有回归。
why: 被砍的字段本来就没携带独有事实，去掉它们只是去掉噪声；grounding 靠的是信息质量，而不是塞进去多少个字段。
why_en: Those fields carried no unique facts, so removing them removed noise, and grounding depends on the quality of the information rather than the number of fields.
whenOtherWins: 如果被砍的字段里有真正独有的事实（比如退货政策原文），那减字段就是在挖掉 grounding，质量一定会掉。
optionMeanings: 把结果归因为换模型。
把实验结论当成解释本身。
声称信息量守恒、只是换了表达。
指出被砍字段本就没有独有信息。
optionMeanings_en: Attributes the result to a model swap.
Treats the experiment's conclusion as the explanation.
Claims information was conserved, only re-expressed.
Points out the removed fields carried no unique information.
optionDirectness: 只有当模型版本确实同期变更时才成立，也毁掉了归因。
指标没动是结果，回答不了「为什么」这个问题。
当确实做了摘要压缩、而不是直接删除时才对。
当被删字段以空值和默认值为主时的真实原因。
optionDirectness_en: Only true if the model version really changed at the same time, which also destroys attribution.
A flat metric is the outcome; it doesn't answer why.
Right only if fields were summarized rather than deleted outright.
The real reason when the deleted fields were mostly empty or default values.
optionScenarioImpacts: 同时动两个变量，实验结论直接不可信。
面试官会追问「所以机制是什么」，我又回到原点。
和事实不符：那些字段是删掉的，不是压缩的。
把产品动作和 grounding 机制连起来，追问也接得住。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Changing two variables at once makes the experiment's conclusion untrustworthy.
They'll ask what the mechanism was and I'm back where I started.
It contradicts the facts: those fields were deleted, not compressed.
It links the product move to the grounding mechanism and survives follow-ups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让回答建立在提供的上下文事实上，而不是模型凭空生成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Grounding means answers are built on the facts provided in context rather than invented.

termDefinitions.meaning: A/B 实验里接受新方案的那一组，对照组叫 control。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The treatment is the A/B group receiving the new version, contrasted with the control group.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次请求里喂给模型的全部文本：指令、检索材料和用户输入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Context is all the text handed to the model in one request: instructions, retrieved material, and user input.

scenario: 教练在复盘里特意教了这组词：面试里说得出「harness」这个词，对方立刻知道你在这一行里待过。
scenario_en: My coach taught this vocabulary on purpose: saying the word "harness" in an interview immediately signals you've actually worked in this space.
q: LLM、harness、agent 这三个词分别指什么？
q_en: What exactly do the words LLM, harness, and agent each refer to?
text: 模型本身只会生成{{下一个 token}}；围在它周围的那一圈上下文、工具描述和调用循环叫 {{harness}}（马具）——有了它才能驾着模型跑向你要的方向。今天的 agent 基本都是{{多轮}}对话循环：一轮解决不了就把新信息接到对话末尾再来一轮。
text_en: The model itself only generates the {{next token}}; the ring of context, tool descriptions, and the calling loop around it is the {{harness}}, which is what lets you steer the model where you want. Today's agents are essentially {{multi-turn}} loops: when one turn isn't enough, new information is appended and another turn runs.
why: 把 LLM 和它外面那一圈分开说，就能干净地回答「你们的 agent 是什么」——模型是引擎，harness 才是我作为工程师真正在设计的东西。
why_en: Separating the model from the ring around it lets me answer "what is your agent" cleanly: the model is the engine, and the harness is what I as an engineer actually design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大语言模型，本质是根据已有文本预测下一个 token 的模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLM stands for large language model, a model that predicts the next token from the text so far.

termDefinitions.meaning: 包在模型外面的那层工程：上下文组装、工具描述、调用循环和终止条件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The harness is the engineering layer around the model: context assembly, tool descriptions, the calling loop, and stopping conditions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型切分文本的最小单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token is the smallest unit a model splits text into.

scenario: 系统设计轮里我说了句「这听起来像一个 agent flow」，面试官接着问：「那你怎么定义 agent？」我需要一句不靠画图的定义。
scenario_en: In the design round I said "this sounds like an agent flow" and the interviewer asked how I define an agent — I need a one-line definition that doesn't rely on a diagram.
q: 怎么用一句话把 agent 和一问一答的 chatbot 区分开？
q_en: In one sentence, how do you separate an agent from a one-shot chatbot?
options: agent 是参数量更大的模型，能力更强所以能处理更复杂的任务，chatbot 用的是小模型
agent 一定是多个模型协同工作的系统，单个模型无论怎么包装都只能算 chatbot
agent 在 harness 里多轮循环：模型可要求调工具，结果回填进对话再继续，直到出终答
agent 就是能联网的 chatbot，区别只在于有没有接上搜索引擎这一个具体的能力
options_en: An agent is a bigger model, so it handles harder tasks, while a chatbot runs on a small one.
An agent is always several models working together; a single model can only ever be a chatbot.
An agent loops in a harness: the model can request tools, results are appended, and it continues until a final answer.
An agent is just a chatbot with internet access; the only difference is whether a search engine is attached.
tradeoff: 多轮 agent 循环 vs 单轮问答：多轮能自己去补缺失的信息，代价是延迟、token 成本和失控风险都随轮数放大。
why: 区别不在模型大小也不在模型个数，而在控制流：agent 允许模型在一次任务里反复要工具、把结果接回对话，直到自己判断可以收尾。
why_en: The difference isn't model size or model count but control flow: an agent lets the model keep asking for tools and folding results back into the conversation until it decides it can finish.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务一轮就能答完（固定 FAQ 查询、格式转换），套上 agent 循环只是白白多花延迟和 token。
optionMeanings: 用模型规模区分。
用模型个数区分。
用控制流与工具循环区分。
用是否联网区分。

Distinguishes by number of models.
Distinguishes by control flow and the tool loop.
Distinguishes by internet access.

联网只是众多工具里的一个，不构成定义。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: An agent is an LLM application that decides on its own to call tools across multiple turns and keeps going based on the results.

scenario: PropTech agentic 岗（Daisy 那轮）面试官说「我们的 agentic 系统已经相当成熟」，点名问 LangChain、LangSmith、LangGraph。我当时完全接不上。
scenario_en: In the PropTech agentic screen the interviewer said "we're quite advanced with our agentic system" and named LangChain, LangSmith and LangGraph. I had nothing.
q: 这三个东西该怎么各用一句话区分开？
q_en: How do you tell these three apart in one line each?
options: LangChain 搭 agent、LangSmith 做 tracing 与评估、LangGraph 是有状态图运行时
LangChain 是一个向量数据库、LangSmith 是它的托管云服务、LangGraph 是可视化流程图编辑器
三者是同一个库的三个版本号，LangGraph 最新，用最新那个就行，功能都是向后兼容的
LangChain 是模型供应商的 SDK、LangSmith 是提示词交易市场、LangGraph 是模型微调工具链
options_en: LangChain builds the agent, LangSmith does tracing and evaluation, LangGraph is the stateful graph runtime.
LangChain is a vector database, LangSmith is its managed cloud service, and LangGraph is a visual flowchart editor.
They're three version numbers of one library; LangGraph is newest, so just use it since everything is backward compatible.
LangChain is a model vendor's SDK, LangSmith is a prompt marketplace, and LangGraph is a fine-tuning toolchain.
tradeoff: 用框架 vs 直接调模型 SDK：框架给现成的工具调用协议和追踪能力，代价是多一层抽象，出问题要穿透它去 debug。
why: 一句话版本：LangChain 是搭 agent 的上层接口，LangGraph 是它底下那台有状态的图运行时，LangSmith 负责把每一次调用记录下来做评估。
why_en: The one-liner is that LangChain is the high-level interface for building agents, LangGraph is the stateful graph runtime underneath it, and LangSmith records every call for evaluation.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方的栈上根本没有 LangChain（自研 harness 或直接调模型 SDK），硬扯这三个名字反而像只会背框架名。
optionMeanings: 按「搭建、观测、运行时」三层分工。
把它们说成存储与云服务。
把它们当成同一个库的版本演进。
把它们说成供应商 SDK 与训练工具。
optionMeanings_en: Splits them into build, observe, and runtime layers.
Describes them as storage and a cloud service.
Treats them as versions of one library.
Describes them as a vendor SDK and training tooling.
optionDirectness: 对方在这套栈上做产品、想确认你能聊起来时的正解。
向量库是另一类组件，和这三个都不重叠。
三者是并存的独立组件，不是版本关系。
微调和提示词市场都不是这三个做的事。
optionDirectness_en: The right answer when they build on this stack and want to know you can hold a conversation.
A vector database is a separate category and overlaps none of the three.
They coexist as separate components, not as versions.
Neither fine-tuning nor a prompt marketplace is what any of them does.

一句就露馅：把编排框架说成了存储层。
会被追问「那你用的是哪个版本」，当场收不了场。
答案和事实无关，等于确认了这块完全空白。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They immediately know I've at least read the docs and can follow the architecture talk.
One line gives it away: calling an orchestration framework a storage layer.
They'll ask which version I used and there's no way to recover.
The answer is unrelated to reality and confirms the gap outright.

termDefinitions.meaning: 构建 LLM 应用与 agent 的上层框架，提供统一的工具调用与模型抽象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LangChain is the high-level framework for building LLM applications and agents with a unified tool-calling and model abstraction.

termDefinitions.meaning: LangChain 的可观测与评估平台，记录每次调用的输入输出用于调试和打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LangSmith is the observability and evaluation platform that records each call's inputs and outputs for debugging and scoring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有状态的图式运行时：节点是函数、边是状态转移，支持 checkpoint 与人工介入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LangGraph is a stateful graph runtime where nodes are functions and edges are transitions, with checkpointing and human-in-the-loop support.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一次调用链路上的每一步记录下来，用于排查和评估。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tracing records every step along one call path so it can be debugged and evaluated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 软件开发工具包，供应商提供的调用其服务的官方库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SDK stands for software development kit, a vendor's official library for calling their service.

scenario: action item：动手写一个至少带一次工具调用的最小 agent，目标是面试里能在 60 秒内说清 LangChain 是什么、我用它做了什么。
scenario_en: Action item: build a minimal agent with at least one tool call, so I can explain in 60 seconds what LangChain is and what I built with it.
q: LangChain 1.0 之后的最小心智模型是什么？
q_en: What is the minimal mental model of LangChain after 1.0?
text: 用 {{create_agent}} 把一个模型和一组 {{tool}} 组装成 agent；它跑在 {{LangGraph}} 运行时上——节点是函数、边是状态转移，checkpoint、流式输出和人工介入都建在这几个概念之上；想在循环中间插手就用 {{middleware}}（日志、护栏、重试）。
text_en: Use {{create_agent}} to assemble a model plus a set of {{tool}} objects into an agent; it runs on the {{LangGraph}} runtime where nodes are functions and edges are transitions, with checkpointing, streaming and human-in-the-loop built on those ideas; to intervene mid-loop you use {{middleware}} for logging, guardrails and retries.
why: 60 秒版本就是这一句：模型加工具组装成 agent，跑在一个图运行时上，需要插手的地方用中间件——不用背整个 API 列表。
why_en: The sixty-second version is exactly this: a model plus tools assembled into an agent, running on a graph runtime, with middleware where you need to intervene — no API list memorization required.

termDefinitions.meaning: LangChain 1.0 里把模型和工具组装成 agent 的入口函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: create_agent is the LangChain 1.0 entry point that assembles a model and tools into an agent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带类型 schema 的外部能力，模型可以选择调用它并读回结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tool is an external capability with a typed schema that the model can choose to call and read results from.

termDefinitions.meaning: 插在 agent 循环各阶段的钩子，用来做日志、改提示、加护栏或重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Middleware are hooks inserted into stages of the agent loop for logging, prompt shaping, guardrails, or retries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把图运行时的状态存下来，使流程能暂停、恢复或回溯。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A checkpoint persists the graph runtime's state so a run can pause, resume, or roll back.

scenario: Daisy 那轮面试官把 Temporal 介绍成他们基础设施的核心，我当场把它误认成了「一个 markdown 文件」。
scenario_en: In the Daisy screen the interviewer introduced Temporal as core infrastructure, and I mistook it for "a markdown file" on the spot.
q: Temporal 一句话是什么东西？
q_en: In one sentence, what is Temporal?
options: 一个消息队列：生产者投递任务、消费者拉取执行，靠重试和死信队列保证任务最终不丢
一个定时任务调度器：按 cron 表达式在指定时刻触发作业，失败了按重试策略自动重跑
持久化执行引擎：每一步记进 event history，崩溃后重放历史恢复现场
一个容器编排平台：把长任务打包成 pod 调度到集群上，节点挂了就在别的节点重新拉起来
options_en: A message queue: producers enqueue tasks, consumers pull and execute, with retries and a dead-letter queue so nothing is lost.
A cron scheduler: it fires jobs at specified times by expression and reruns them by retry policy on failure.
A durable execution engine: each step is written to an event history and replayed after a crash to restore state.
A container orchestrator: it packages long jobs as pods onto a cluster and reschedules them elsewhere when a node dies.
tradeoff: Temporal vs 队列加重试：Temporal 保住的是「跑到一半的进度」，代价是工作流代码必须确定性可重放，还多一套服务要运维。
why: 队列保的是「这条消息还在」，Temporal 保的是「这个流程执行到第几步、拿到过哪些结果」——崩溃后不用从头再跑一遍。
why_en: A queue guarantees the message still exists, while Temporal guarantees the workflow's progress and past results survive, so a crash doesn't send you back to step one.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务只跑几秒、失败了整体重试也没有副作用，一个带重试的队列就够了，没必要引入一整套编排引擎。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["workflow 开始执行"] --> B["每步写入 event history"]
  B --> C["进程崩溃"]
  C --> D["worker 重放 history"]
  D --> E["恢复到崩溃前状态 继续执行"]

把它理解成定时触发器。
把它理解成可重放的执行引擎。
把它理解成集群调度层。

Reads it as a time-based trigger.
Reads it as a replayable execution engine.
Reads it as a cluster scheduling layer.

cron 决定「什么时候开始」，管不了「中途崩了怎么办」。
抓住了 durable execution 这个核心概念。
编排的是进程和容器，不是业务流程的中间状态。
optionDirectness_en: A queue keeps the message but not the workflow's position.
Cron decides when to start, not what happens after a mid-run crash.
It captures the core idea of durable execution.
It schedules processes and containers, not a business workflow's intermediate state.

把长流程的容错说成了触发时机，答非所问。
接得住下一问「workflow 和 activity 有什么区别」。
pod 重启后业务流程照样从头开始，没解决问题。

It turns fault tolerance for long flows into a question of trigger timing.
It sets up the next question about workflows versus activities.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个持久化执行引擎：把长流程的每一步写进历史，崩溃后重放历史恢复执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Temporal is a durable execution engine that records each step of a long workflow and replays that history to resume after a crash.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持久化执行：保证一段流程即使经历崩溃和重启也能跑到完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Durable execution guarantees a workflow runs to completion even across crashes and restarts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次工作流执行的完整事件日志，是恢复状态的唯一依据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The event history is the complete log of one workflow execution and the sole basis for restoring its state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按时间表达式定时触发任务的调度方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cron is a scheduling convention that triggers jobs on a time expression.

termDefinitions.meaning: 反复处理失败的消息被移入的专用队列，等待人工介入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dead-letter queue holds messages that repeatedly failed processing, waiting for manual intervention.

scenario: 面试官继续追问：「那你会怎么用 Temporal 写一个多步骤的长流程？」我需要知道它的两层分工。
scenario_en: The follow-up: "So how would you write a multi-step long-running flow in Temporal?" I need to know its two-layer split.
q: Temporal 里 workflow 和 activity 各自负责什么？
q_en: What do workflows and activities each own in Temporal?
text: {{workflow}} 是确定性、可重放的编排代码，负责「下一步做什么」，本身不能直接产生副作用；{{activity}} 才是真正调外部 API、写数据库的那一步，失败按重试策略自动重跑。崩溃恢复靠重放 {{event history}}，把状态放回崩溃前那一刻再继续。
text_en: A {{workflow}} is deterministic, replayable orchestration code that decides what happens next and performs no side effects itself; an {{activity}} is the step that actually calls an external API or writes a database, retried automatically on failure. Recovery replays the {{event history}} to restore the state just before the crash and continue.
why: 分层的理由是可重放性：编排代码每次重放都必须走出同一条路径，所以所有不确定的副作用都要被赶进 activity 里。
why_en: The split exists for replayability: orchestration code must take the same path every replay, so every nondeterministic side effect is pushed into an activity.

termDefinitions.meaning: Temporal 里描述流程步骤顺序的确定性代码，可以被反复重放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A workflow in Temporal is deterministic code describing the order of steps, and it can be replayed repeatedly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 工作流里真正执行副作用的一步：调 API、写库、发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An activity is the step inside a workflow that performs real side effects such as API calls, database writes, or sending messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同样的输入每次都走出同样的执行路径，重放才能得到一致结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Determinism means the same input always takes the same execution path, which is what makes replay consistent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次工作流执行的完整事件日志。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The event history is the complete log of one workflow execution.

scenario: Alterion 技术轮问「你 React Context 熟吗」，我答了「I think I'll be able to handle it」——一个用了两年的核心 API，这句话当场被判红旗。
scenario_en: In the Alterion technical round I answered "I think I'll be able to handle it" about React Context — a core API I've used for two years, and it was flagged as a red flag.
q: 这句话该换成什么？
q_en: What should that sentence be replaced with?
options: 「我平时主要用 Redux 做状态管理，Context 用得比较少，不过概念相通，上手应该很快」
「createContext 建 context、useContext 读它，跨树共享、免 prop drilling」
「Context 就是 React 里的全局变量，挂上去所有组件都能拿到，跟往 window 上挂一个对象是一个意思」
「我在项目里用过 Context，具体 API 记不太清了，真要写的时候查一下官方文档就行」
options_en: "I mostly use Redux for state, so I don't reach for Context often, but the concepts overlap and I'd pick it up fast."
"createContext creates a context, useContext reads it: shared state across the tree, no prop drilling."
"Context is React's global variable — put a value on it and every component can read it, same as hanging an object on window."
"I've used Context on projects, I don't remember the exact API, but I'd just check the docs when I actually need to write it."
tradeoff: Context vs 状态管理库：Context 零依赖、适合主题和登录态这类低频值，代价是 value 一变整棵消费子树都会重渲。
why: 对一个用了两年的核心 API，含糊等于自我否定；一句「createContext 加 useContext，跨树共享、免 prop drilling」就足够，还能顺势带出典型场景。
why_en: Hedging on an API I've used for two years reads as self-doubt, and one line — createContext plus useContext to share state across the tree without prop drilling — is enough to close it.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方问的是「你们为什么选 Context 而不是状态库」，那就该讲取舍：低频全局值适合 Context，高频更新会拖垮整棵子树。
optionMeanings: 改口说自己主要用别的方案。
直接给出 API 名与它解决的问题。
用「全局变量」做类比。
承认记不清并交给文档。
optionMeanings_en: Deflects by saying I mainly use something else.
States the API names and the problem they solve.
Uses a "global variable" analogy.
Admits not remembering and defers to the docs.
optionDirectness: 只有当我确实没用过 Context 时才诚实，但这里不成立。
对方要确认基础功底扎实时的标准回答。
类比抹掉了 Provider 作用域和重渲行为，会被追问戳破。
对核心 API 说记不清，等于坐实了那个红旗。
optionDirectness_en: Honest only if I truly hadn't used Context, which isn't the case here.
The standard answer when they're checking that fundamentals are solid.
The analogy erases provider scoping and re-render behavior and won't survive a follow-up.
Saying you forget a core API confirms exactly the red flag.

十秒内证明基础扎实，话题可以往上层推进。
下一问「Provider 的作用范围呢」立刻接不住。
红旗从「犹豫」升级成「确实不会」。

Ten seconds proves the fundamentals and the conversation can move up a level.

The red flag upgrades from hesitation to a confirmed gap.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Prop drilling is the chore of passing props down through every intermediate component just to reach a deep one.
