scenario: action item 要求：五个常用 hook，每个都要能在 10 秒内说清它是干什么的，不能犹豫。
scenario_en: The action item: for each of the five common hooks, be able to say what it does in ten seconds with no hedging.
q: useState / useEffect / useCallback / useMemo / useRef 各是干什么的？
q_en: What does each of useState, useEffect, useCallback, useMemo, and useRef do?
text: {{useState}} 给组件一块会触发重渲的状态；{{useEffect}} 把渲染之外的副作用（订阅、请求、手动 DOM 操作）挂到渲染之后执行；useCallback 缓存{{函数}}引用、useMemo 缓存{{计算结果}}，都是为了让下游依赖不白白失效；{{useRef}} 存一个改了也不触发重渲的可变盒子。
text_en: {{useState}} gives a component state that triggers re-renders; {{useEffect}} runs side effects such as subscriptions, requests and manual DOM work after render; useCallback caches a {{function}} reference and useMemo caches a {{computed value}} so downstream dependencies don't invalidate for nothing; {{useRef}} holds a mutable box whose changes never trigger a re-render.
why: 记忆抓手是「会不会触发重渲」：useState 会、useRef 不会；useMemo 和 useCallback 都不改渲染结果，只是让引用在依赖不变时保持稳定。
why_en: The hook to remember them by is whether they trigger a re-render: useState does, useRef doesn't, and useMemo and useCallback only keep references stable when dependencies haven't changed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存一个跨渲染保留、修改时不触发重渲的可变引用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: useRef stores a mutable reference that persists across renders and never triggers a re-render when changed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 渲染纯计算之外的事：订阅、发请求、改 DOM、设定时器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A side effect is anything outside pure render computation: subscribing, fetching, touching the DOM, setting timers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 告诉 hook「这些值变了才重新执行或重新计算」的那个数组。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The dependency array tells a hook which values must change before it re-runs or recomputes.

scenario: 一个列表组件在父组件每次重渲时都整体重画：一个昂贵的过滤计算被重跑、一个传给子组件的回调每次都是新引用、还有一个定时器 id 需要跨渲染保存。
scenario_en: A list component fully repaints on every parent render: an expensive filter recomputes, a callback passed to a child is a new reference each time, and a timer id must survive across renders.
q: 这三件事分别该用哪个 hook？
q_en: Which hook handles each of these three?
options: 过滤用 useCallback、回调用 useMemo、定时器 id 用 useState 存起来
过滤用 useMemo、回调用 useCallback、定时器 id 用 useRef
三件事都用 useState 存起来，在 useEffect 里同步更新，引用自然就稳定了
三件事都用 useRef 存，ref 改了不会触发重渲，这是最省渲染次数的做法
options_en: useCallback for the filter, useMemo for the callback, useState for the timer id.
useMemo for the filter, useCallback for the callback, useRef for the timer id.
Put all three in useState and sync them in useEffect so the references stay stable.
Put all three in useRef since ref changes never re-render, which is the cheapest option.
tradeoff: 加缓存 hook vs 不加：缓存换掉重复计算和引用抖动，代价是多了依赖数组这个新的出错面。
why: 分工是按「缓存的是什么」定的：useMemo 缓存值、useCallback 缓存函数、useRef 存一个和渲染无关的可变盒子。
why_en: The split follows what's being cached: useMemo caches a value, useCallback caches a function, and useRef holds a mutable box that has nothing to do with rendering.
whenOtherWins: 如果子组件没有被 memo 包住、或者那个计算本来就很便宜，加 useCallback 和 useMemo 只是徒增依赖数组的维护成本。
optionMeanings: 把三个 hook 的职责两两互换。
按缓存对象把三件事各归其位。
全部塞进状态并靠 effect 同步。
全部塞进 ref 以避免重渲。
optionMeanings_en: Swaps the responsibilities of the hooks around.
Assigns each case by what is being cached.
Puts everything in state and syncs via effect.
Puts everything in refs to avoid re-renders.
optionDirectness: useCallback 缓存的是函数，用它包一个计算结果不对路。
值、函数、跨渲染可变量三类各有对应 hook。
把派生值变成状态，会多一次渲染且容易不同步。
ref 变化不触发重渲，过滤结果改了界面不会更新。
optionDirectness_en: useCallback caches functions, so wrapping a computed value with it is the wrong tool.
Values, functions, and cross-render mutables each have their own hook.
Turning derived values into state adds a render and invites desync.
Ref changes don't re-render, so an updated filter result never reaches the screen.
optionScenarioImpacts: 过滤照样每次重跑，回调引用照样每次都变。
昂贵计算只在依赖变时重算，子组件不再无谓重渲。
多绕一圈 effect，还可能渲染出上一帧的旧值。
界面不再跟随数据更新，等于把 bug 换了个形式。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The filter still recomputes and the callback reference still changes every render.
The expensive computation only reruns when dependencies change and the child stops re-rendering.
An extra effect hop, plus the risk of rendering last frame's stale value.
The UI stops following the data, which just relocates the bug.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在依赖不变时复用上一次的计算结果，避免重复的昂贵计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: useMemo reuses the previous computed result while dependencies are unchanged, avoiding repeated expensive work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在依赖不变时复用同一个函数引用，避免子组件因引用变化而重渲。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: useCallback reuses the same function reference while dependencies are unchanged, so children don't re-render on identity changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 包住组件，让 props 浅比较相同时跳过重渲。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: memo wraps a component so it skips re-rendering when a shallow props comparison finds no change.

termDefinitions.meaning: 可以从现有状态算出来的值，不该单独再存一份状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A derived value can be computed from existing state and should not be stored as separate state.

options: useState 加受控表单：value 绑 state、onChange 回写，提交前能就地校验
useEffect 加 fetch：显式画出 loading 和 error 两个分支，不只写成功路径

useEffect with fetch: explicitly render the loading and error branches, not just the success path.
Conditional rendering plus .map() list rendering with a stable key on each item so edits don't shuffle rows.

scenario_en: Live coding task: fetch a task list from an API on mount and render it. Thirty minutes on the clock, and the interviewer specifically watches for the non-success paths.
q: 这段 useEffect 最容易被扣分的地方是什么？
q_en: Where does this useEffect most easily lose points?
options: 只写了成功分支：没有 loading、没有 error 兜底，也没在卸载时取消响应
没有把 fetch 逻辑抽成自定义 hook，组件文件越写越长、换个页面没法复用
没有用 useMemo 缓存返回的数组，每次重渲都生成新引用，被 memo 包住的子组件也跟着白白重画
没有把请求放进 useLayoutEffect，首屏会先闪一下空白再把内容补上来
options_en: Only the success branch exists: no loading state, no error fallback, and no cancellation of a stale response on unmount.
The fetch logic isn't extracted into a custom hook, so the file grows and nothing is reusable on another page.
The returned array isn't wrapped in useMemo, so a memo-wrapped child repaints on every render for nothing.
The request isn't in useLayoutEffect, so the first paint flashes blank before the content arrives.
tradeoff: 手写 useEffect 加 fetch vs 用数据请求库：手写能展示我懂生命周期和竞态，代价是取消、错误态、重试全要自己写。
why: 异步请求有三种状态，写全 loading、error、success 才是完整答案；卸载时不取消，慢响应回来会往已经消失的组件里写状态。
why_en: An async request has three states, so loading, error and success all need rendering, and without cancellation a slow response writes into a component that no longer exists.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试明说用 React Query 或 SWR 这类数据请求库，loading 和 error 由库给出，重点就转到缓存 key 和失效策略上。

scenario: GenLogs recruiter 问：「你有 AWS 或 Azure 经验吗？」我在 Meta 和 TikTok 用的都是公司自研的内部云，没碰过公有云控制台。
scenario_en: The GenLogs recruiter asked whether I have AWS or Azure experience. At Meta and TikTok I used in-house private clouds and have never touched a public cloud console.
q: 怎么答既诚实又不掉分？
q_en: How do I answer honestly without losing ground?
options: 「我在 Meta 和 TikTok 有云经验」——先把有经验三个字说出去，等对方追问具体服务名再随机应变
「没直接用过 AWS；我用的是 Meta 和 TikTok 的内部私有云，核心概念是同一套」
「没用过，但我学得很快」——简短承认就打住，不展开，尽快把话题推回我熟悉的项目上去
「我有云经验」，紧接着补一句「虽然我没真正用过 AWS，不过我会很快学会的」——两句连着说
options_en: "I have cloud experience from Meta and TikTok" — lead with the claim and improvise once they ask for service names.
"I haven't used AWS directly; at Meta and TikTok I worked on internal private clouds, and autoscaling, container orchestration and monitoring are the same concepts."
"I haven't used it, but I learn fast" — a short admission, no elaboration, then steer back to familiar projects.
"I have cloud experience," immediately followed by "though I've never actually used AWS, I'll pick it up fast" — both in a row.
tradeoff: bridge 到内部私有云 vs 直接说没用过：bridge 保住了「我懂云的核心概念」，代价是后面每一句都不能再自相矛盾。
why: 顺序是先明确说没直接用过公有云，再桥到内部私有云的同构概念；顺序反了就是自相矛盾，那比不会更扣分。
why_en: The order matters: state clearly that I haven't used the public cloud, then bridge to the equivalent concepts in the internal cloud, because the reverse order sounds self-contradictory.
whenOtherWins: 如果 JD 硬性要求某个具体服务的实操经验（比如「必须做过 EKS 生产运维」），坦白差距加一个学习计划比 bridge 更可信。

先划清边界，再桥到同构的内部经验。
承认没有并快速转移话题。
先声称有经验，再当场自己否定。
optionMeanings_en: Claim experience first and leave details until pressed.
Draw the boundary first, then bridge to equivalent internal experience.
Admit the gap and change the subject quickly.
Claim experience, then contradict it in the next breath.
optionDirectness: 只有当我确实有公有云实操经历时才成立。
有可类比的内部经验、且能说出具体概念时的做法。
当对方明显不在意这项、只是走流程时够用。
两句话方向相反，任何前提下都站不住。
optionDirectness_en: Only holds if I really do have hands-on public cloud experience.
The move when comparable internal experience exists and I can name the concepts.
Enough when the recruiter clearly doesn't care and is just checking a box.
The two sentences point opposite ways and hold under no premise.

对方听到的是「概念齐了，只差 API 名字」。
把一个可以转化的差距直接留成了空白。
对方记住的是「他刚才说的不实」，比没经验更糟。

They hear "the concepts are there, only the API names are missing."
It leaves a convertible gap as a plain blank.

scenario_en: Asked about a tool I've never used — Temporal, LangChain, C#, and AWS have all come up. This template has to be automatic.
q: 把「不熟悉的工具」bridge 模板的四段排成正确顺序。
q_en: Put the four beats of the unfamiliar-tool bridge template in the right order.
steps: 说清我理解的这个工具核心是什么，用我自己的话，而不是背它主页上的介绍

q_en: What should the bridge sentence rest on?
options: 「我朋友从 Java 转 C# 说两周就上手了，所以我估计我也差不多，学习曲线应该不算陡」

「我最近在自学 C#，官方文档前几章看完了，正在跟着做一个练手项目，下周应该能跑起来」

"No C#, but I have Java experience — both strongly typed and class-based with comparably mature ecosystems, so a few weeks to be productive."

scenario: Amazon Round 2 讲 P99 故事：我调用下游 catalog 校验团队的 API，他们发新版本把超时从 500ms 改成 2s，把我这边打挂了。我当场把上下游说反了。
scenario_en: Telling the P99 story in Amazon Round 2: I call the catalog validation team's API, they shipped a release moving the timeout from 500ms to 2s and broke my service — and I got upstream and downstream backwards on the spot.
q: 在这段依赖关系里，谁是谁的 upstream？
q_en: In this dependency, who is upstream of whom?
options: 我是他们的 downstream，他们是我的 upstream——我依赖谁谁就在上游
我是他们的 upstream，因为请求是从我这边发起的，数据流也是从我流向他们那边的
看数据流向：响应从他们流回我，所以我是下游；但因为我发起调用，我同时也是上游
两边互为上下游，因为这是双向调用关系，这个词在微服务里没有固定方向
options_en: I am their downstream and they are my upstream — whoever I depend on sits upstream of me.
I'm their upstream because the request starts on my side and data flows from me to them.
Follow the data: responses flow from them to me so I'm downstream, but since I initiate the call I'm also upstream.
Both are upstream of each other since calls go both ways; the word has no fixed direction in microservices.
why: 方向由依赖决定，不由谁先发包决定：我调用他们的 API，所以我在下游；反过来别人依赖我的服务，我就是他们的 upstream。
why_en: Direction is set by dependency, not by who sends the first packet: I call their API so I'm downstream, and whoever depends on my service has me as their upstream.
optionMeanings: 按依赖方向判定。
按请求发起方判定。
按数据流向判定并自我矛盾。
认为方向不确定。
optionMeanings_en: Decides by dependency direction.
Decides by who initiates the request.
Decides by data flow and contradicts itself.
Claims the direction is undefined.
optionDirectness: 这就是行业里说这两个词时的默认含义。
发起方向和上下游无关，这正是我上次说反的原因。
同一个服务不可能既在上游又在下游。
确实存在互相调用的情况，但每条依赖边的方向仍然是明确的。
optionDirectness_en: This is what the industry means by default when using these two words.
Who initiates has nothing to do with it, which is exactly why I got it backwards.
One service can't be both upstream and downstream on the same edge.
Mutual calls do exist, but each dependency edge still has a definite direction.
optionScenarioImpacts: 「他们发版影响到下游」这句话就说得准了。
故事里的责任方会被说反，听的人要停下来重建关系。
面试官会花时间澄清词义，故事节奏断掉。
等于承认自己没有稳定的依赖关系词汇。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The line "their release broke their downstream" finally comes out right.
The story names the wrong party and the listener has to stop and rebuild the map.
The interviewer spends time clarifying vocabulary and the story loses its rhythm.
It amounts to admitting I lack stable vocabulary for dependencies.

termDefinitions.meaning: 我依赖的那一方：我调用它的接口，它的变更会传导到我这里。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Upstream is the side I depend on: I call its interface, and its changes propagate to me.

termDefinitions.meaning: 依赖我的那一方：我发新版本会影响到它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Downstream is the side that depends on me: my releases affect it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 99 分位延迟：100 次请求里最慢的那 1 次达到的耗时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: P99 is the 99th-percentile latency, the level reached by the slowest one request in a hundred.

scenario: Apple 面试官直接问「Java 熟练度 1 到 10 打几分」，我自评 7；这个团队日常就用 Java，下一轮很可能要现场写。
scenario_en: The Apple interviewer asked me to rate my Java from one to ten and I said seven; the team codes in Java daily and the next round may well be live Java.
q: 两周时间里复习什么最止血？
q_en: With two weeks, what review actually stops the bleeding?
options: 把 JVM 垃圾回收算法、G1 与 ZGC 的分代策略从头到尾看一遍，在深度上直接压过面试官
刷 200 道 LeetCode 的 Java 版本，把语法在算法题里练熟，业务框架先放一边完全不管
写一个最小 Spring Boot 服务：REST 端点收请求、JPA 存取、@Transactional 划事务边界
背 Java 八股：HashMap 扩容机制、synchronized 锁升级、ThreadLocal 内存泄漏这些高频考点
options_en: Read through JVM garbage collection, G1 and ZGC generation strategies end to end and out-depth the interviewer.
Grind 200 LeetCode problems in Java to drill syntax through algorithms and ignore application frameworks entirely.
Build a minimal Spring Boot service: a REST endpoint for requests, JPA for persistence, @Transactional for the transaction boundary.
Memorize the classic Java trivia: HashMap resizing, synchronized lock escalation, ThreadLocal memory leaks.
tradeoff: 补框架实操 vs 补语言八股：写一个能跑的 Spring Boot 服务直接对应「这个团队每天用 Java 做什么」，代价是深层原理题会答得浅。
why: 风险不在语法，而在「团队日常怎么用 Java」；把 REST、持久化、事务边界这条主链路手写一遍，现场写代码时才不是冷的。
why_en: The risk isn't syntax but how this team uses Java day to day, so hand-writing the REST, persistence, and transaction path once is what keeps a live round from starting cold.
whenOtherWins: 如果那一轮明说是纯算法轮（LeetCode 风格），那语法手感和标准库 API 反而比 Spring 更该先补。
optionMeanings: 补运行时与垃圾回收原理。
用算法题练语法手感。
手写一遍业务主链路。
背高频原理面试题。
optionMeanings_en: Study runtime and garbage collection internals.
Drill syntax through algorithm problems.
Hand-write the core application path once.
Memorize common internals questions.
optionDirectness: 当岗位真的是 JVM 调优方向时才是首选。
当那一轮确实是纯算法轮时才够用。
当团队日常写业务服务、且可能现场写代码时的首选。
当面试风格偏原理问答时才有性价比。
optionDirectness_en: The first choice only when the role really is JVM tuning.
Enough only when that round truly is pure algorithms.
The first choice when the team writes application services and may ask for live code.
Worth the time only when the interview style leans toward internals Q&A.

语法顺了，但被问「你怎么定事务边界」还是空白。
REST、持久化、事务这条主链路一次跑通，追问也有落点。
答得出定义，写不出一个能跑的接口。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Two weeks spent on depth I won't use, and live application code still stalls.
Syntax gets smooth, but "how do you set transaction boundaries" is still blank.
The REST, persistence and transaction path runs once, so follow-ups have somewhere to land.
I can recite definitions but can't write one working endpoint.

termDefinitions.meaning: Java 生态里约定优于配置的应用框架，几行注解就能起一个 HTTP 服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Spring Boot is a convention-over-configuration Java framework that starts an HTTP service from a few annotations.

termDefinitions.meaning: Java 的对象关系映射规范，把实体类映射成数据库表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JPA stands for Java Persistence API, the object-relational mapping standard that maps entity classes to database tables.

scenario: Apple 技术轮前的最小复习目标：能口述一个 Spring Boot REST 服务从收请求到落库的完整链路。
scenario_en: Minimum prep goal before the Apple technical round: narrate a Spring Boot REST service end to end, from receiving a request to writing the database.
q: Spring Boot 从收请求到落库的最小闭环是什么？
q_en: What is the minimal loop of a Spring Boot service from request to database?
text: {{@RestController}} 把一个类暴露成 HTTP 端点，@GetMapping/@PostMapping 绑定路径和方法；持久层写一个继承自 JPA 的 {{Repository}} 接口，Spring 在运行时按方法名生成实现；写操作用 {{@Transactional}} 划事务边界——方法正常返回就提交，抛出运行时异常就整体{{回滚}}。
text_en: {{@RestController}} exposes a class as HTTP endpoints with @GetMapping and @PostMapping binding paths and methods; persistence is a {{Repository}} interface extending JPA whose implementation Spring generates from method names at runtime; writes use {{@Transactional}} to mark the transaction boundary, committing on normal return and {{rolling back}} entirely on a runtime exception.
why: 这条链路是 Java 后端面试的默认起点：说得出注解在哪一层生效，追问「事务边界放哪里」「为什么这里会回滚」才接得住。
why_en: This path is the default starting point in a Java backend interview, and knowing which layer each annotation acts on is what lets me answer where transaction boundaries go and why a rollback happens.

termDefinitions.meaning: Spring 注解，把类里的方法暴露成返回 JSON 的 HTTP 端点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: @RestController is a Spring annotation exposing a class's methods as HTTP endpoints that return JSON.

termDefinitions.meaning: 声明式事务注解：方法正常结束提交，抛运行时异常则整体回滚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: @Transactional declares a transaction that commits when the method returns normally and rolls back on a runtime exception.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持久层接口，Spring Data 根据方法名自动生成查询实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A repository is a persistence interface whose query implementations Spring Data generates from method names.

termDefinitions.meaning: Java 的对象关系映射规范。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JPA stands for Java Persistence API, Java's object-relational mapping standard.

scenario: Amazon onsite loop：Round 3 是 Selling Assistant 的 HM，Round 4 是 AWS 另一个组的资深工程师。教练判断 Round 4 很可能就是 bar raiser。
scenario_en: Amazon onsite loop: Round 3 was the Selling Assistant hiring manager and Round 4 a senior engineer from a different AWS org, which my coach read as the likely bar raiser.
q: bar raiser 在一个 loop 里是什么角色？
q_en: What role does a bar raiser play in a loop?
options: HR 派来的流程监督员，只负责记录时间、确认题目合规，不参与技术评价，也不参与最终投票
来自招聘团队之外、经过专门训练的志愿者，负责横向定级把关和一场公平的复盘
本组最资深的工程师，因为最懂业务，所以由他来定候选人进来之后具体做哪个方向
候选人未来的 skip-level 经理，组织架构上是 HM 的上级，负责给这个 offer 定薪资
options_en: An HR-appointed process monitor who only tracks timing and question compliance, joining neither the technical assessment nor the final vote.
A trained volunteer from outside the hiring team who guards the leveling bar and runs a fair debrief.
The most senior engineer on the hiring team, who decides what the candidate will work on after joining.
The candidate's future skip-level manager, organizationally above the hiring manager and responsible for setting the offer.
why: 公开资料一致的三点：来自招聘团队之外（避开本组 bias）、经过专门训练的志愿者、对「这次录用有没有拉高这条线」负责；多数公开说法还提到他对 HM 有否决权。
why_en: Public sources agree on three things: they come from outside the hiring team to avoid its bias, they are trained volunteers, and they own whether this hire raises the bar.
optionMeanings: 把角色理解成流程合规监督。
外组受训志愿者，负责定级与公平复盘。
把角色理解成本组的技术权威。
把角色理解成管理链上的审批人。
optionMeanings_en: Reads the role as process compliance oversight.
A trained outside volunteer who owns leveling and a fair debrief.
Reads the role as the team's technical authority.
Reads the role as an approver in the management chain.
optionDirectness: 复盘确实要主持，但他同时给出实质性的技术评价。
对上 Round 4 来自外组这个观察，也解释了他为什么问得更宽。
本组最资深的人通常正是要被制衡的那一方。
定薪走的是招聘流程，不是这个角色的职责。
optionDirectness_en: They do run the debrief, but they also give substantive technical assessment.
It matches the observation that Round 4 came from another org and explains the broader questions.
The team's most senior engineer is usually the party being balanced, not the balancer.
Compensation runs through the recruiting process, not this role.
optionScenarioImpacts: 会低估 Round 4，把它当成走过场。
知道 Round 4 在做横向比较，答案要拉到公司层面而非本组细节。
会误以为 Round 4 在挑我进哪个方向，答偏成兴趣匹配。
会误以为要在那轮谈薪资和层级。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: I'd underestimate Round 4 and treat it as a formality.
Knowing it's a cross-company comparison, I pitch answers at company level rather than team detail.
I'd mistake it for team matching and drift into interest fit.
I'd wrongly bring up compensation and level in that round.

termDefinitions.meaning: Amazon 招聘流程里来自招聘团队之外的受训面试官，负责把关录用标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bar raiser is a trained Amazon interviewer from outside the hiring team who guards the hiring standard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 招聘经理，这个岗位未来的直属上级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HM stands for hiring manager, the candidate's future direct manager.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次 onsite 里连续进行的多轮面试的总称。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A loop is the full set of back-to-back interviews in one onsite.

termDefinitions.meaning: 上级的上级，即隔一层的经理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A skip-level manager is your manager's manager, one level removed.

scenario: 同一个 loop 里，招聘团队已经缺人缺了半年、急着补；bar raiser 来自一个完全无关的组，此前和这个岗位没有任何关系。
scenario_en: In the same loop, the hiring team has been short-staffed for six months and is eager to fill the role, while the bar raiser comes from an unrelated org with no stake in it.
q: 把把关人放在招聘团队之外，是在防什么？
q_en: What does placing the gatekeeper outside the hiring team protect against?
options: 防的是候选人作弊：外组的人拿不到本组的题库，题目就不会提前泄漏出去
防的是排期冲突：外组的人日程更空，能保证 loop 的五轮都排得开、不用改期
防的是本组的招聘偏差：急着补人时容易放松标准，外组的人没有这份压力
防的是薪资越权：外组的人不了解本组预算，所以不会随口承诺薪资范围
options_en: Cheating: someone from another org can't access the team's question bank, so questions don't leak in advance.
Scheduling conflicts: an outsider has a lighter calendar, so all five rounds fit without rescheduling.
The hiring team's own bias: teams in a hurry to fill a seat relax the bar, and an outsider carries no such pressure.
Compensation overreach: an outsider doesn't know the team's budget, so they won't promise a salary range.
why: 本组对候选人天然有 bias——缺人越久越容易「先招进来再说」；把一个没有交付压力的外部人放进来，才守得住「和公司内部同级相当」这条横向标准。
why_en: The hiring team is naturally biased because a long-vacant seat pushes toward "hire now and figure it out," so an outsider with no delivery pressure is what holds the cross-company bar.
optionMeanings: 把动机理解成防题目泄漏。
把动机理解成排期便利。
把动机理解成抵消本组的招聘偏差。
把动机理解成薪资权限隔离。
optionMeanings_en: Reads the motive as leak prevention.
Reads the motive as scheduling convenience.
Reads the motive as offsetting the hiring team's bias.
Reads the motive as separating compensation authority.
optionDirectness: 题库保密靠流程管控，和面试官来自哪个组无关。
排期是执行细节，撑不起一个专门设立的角色。
解释了为什么这个角色必须独立于用人团队。
定薪本来就不在面试官手里，无需靠换组来隔离。
optionDirectness_en: Question confidentiality is handled by process, not by which org an interviewer belongs to.
Scheduling is an execution detail and can't justify a dedicated role.
It explains why the role must be independent of the hiring team.
Interviewers never set compensation, so no org separation is needed for it.
optionScenarioImpacts: 把一个定级机制误解成保密机制。
会低估这一轮的权重，准备强度就跟着降下来。
明白这一轮是在和公司内同级横向比，答案要给可迁移的判断。
会误以为这轮能谈薪，把时间浪费在错误的话题上。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It mistakes a leveling mechanism for a confidentiality one.
I'd underweight the round and prepare for it less seriously.
Knowing it's a cross-company comparison, I give transferable judgment rather than team trivia.
I'd wrongly think salary is on the table and waste time on the wrong topic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 来自招聘团队之外的受训面试官，负责把关录用标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bar raiser is a trained interviewer from outside the hiring team who guards the hiring standard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统性的判断偏差，这里指用人团队因为急需补人而放松标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Bias here is the systematic tendency of a short-staffed team to relax its standard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判断候选人对应公司内部的哪一个职级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Leveling decides which internal job level a candidate maps to.
